01Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

The one-line change that reduced clone times by 99% at Pinterest

Pinterest pe git clone karne me kitna time lagta tha? Bahut zyada — repo itna bada tha ki clone karte-karte chai thandi ho jati thi. Phir ek engineer ne ek line badli — aur clone time 99% kam ho gaya. Ye kahani hai ki kaise ek chhoti samajh badi problem solve karti hai.

1. Problem kya thi? — bori wali kahani

Socho tumhe ek bori me se ek aam chahiye. Lekin dukaan wala poori bori hi utha ke de deta hai — 100 kilo ki bori, sirf ek aam ke liye! Git clone bhi wahi kar raha tha: Pinterest ka repo bahut bada tha (saara history, saari branches, saari files) — aur har developer ko poora repo clone karna padta tha, chahe use sirf latest code chahiye ho. Ek line badal ke bataya gaya 'sirf latest code do, poora history mat do' — aur clone 99% fast ho gaya.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Badi problem ka solution aksar chhota hota hai — bas problem ki jad samajhni padti hai. Pinterest ne clone me history download karna band kar diya.

2. Ek line ne kya badla

Problem, solution aur uske peeche ki samajh — tabs me samjho.

Problem — clone bahut slow tha

Pinterest ka monorepo bahut bada tha — saalon ka history, hazaaron commits, badi files. Har naya developer ya CI job git clone karta to poora history download hota — gigabytes ka data. Clone me kai minute lagte the — developer ka time waste, CI slow, aur naye logon ki onboarding mushkil. Example: tumhe sirf aaj ka code chahiye, lekin git tumhe 5 saal ka history bhi de raha hai — wo bhi har baar. Note: bade repos me ye problem common hai — Google, Meta sabke monorepos me hoti hai.

Sahi tareeka: Bade repo me clone time ko measure karna — pehle problem ko samjho.
Galat tareeka: Clone slow hai to bas 'network slow hai' kehna — asal problem history hai.

Solution — ek line: --depth 1

Solution tha shallow clone: git clone --depth 1 — matlab sirf latest commit download karo, poora history mat do. Ek line (ya ek flag) badla — aur clone time 99% kam ho gaya (minutes se seconds me). Example: CI jobs ko sirf latest code chahiye hota hai — history ki zaroorat nahi. Shallow clone se CI bhi fast ho gaya. Note: --depth 1 me tum purana history nahi dekh sakte — lekin CI aur naye developers ko uski zaroorat bhi nahi hoti.

Sahi tareeka: CI aur fresh clones me --depth 1 use karna.
Galat tareeka: Har jagah shallow clone use karna — jahan history chahiye (git log, blame) wahan nahi chalega.

Kyun kaam kiya — history hi problem thi

Git clone me sabse zyada time history download karne me lagta hai — har commit, har file ka har version. Latest code to chhota hota hai — history hi gigabytes ki hoti hai. Example: repo ka latest code 100MB hai, history 10GB hai — clone me 99% time history me jata hai. --depth 1 ne wahi 99% kaat diya. Lesson: problem ko measure karo — pata karo time kahan ja raha hai, phir wahi fix karo. Pinterest ne pehle measure kiya, phir ek line badli.

Sahi tareeka: Pehle measure karo time kahan ja raha hai, phir fix karo.
Galat tareeka: Bina measure kiye random optimization karna — time waste hoga.

Aur tareeke — partial clone aur sparse checkout

Shallow clone ke alawa do aur tareeke hain: Partial clone (--filter=blob:none) — history lo, lekin files tab download karo jab zaroorat ho. Sparse checkout — repo ka sirf ek hissa checkout karo, poora nahi. Example: monorepo me 100 projects hain, tumhe sirf 1 chahiye — sparse checkout se sirf wo 1 milega. Note: ye teeno techniques bade repos ke liye hain — chhote repos me zaroorat nahi padti. Lesson: tool ko samajh ke use karo — git me bahut se hidden features hain.

Sahi tareeka: Bade monorepo me partial clone ya sparse checkout try karna.
Galat tareeka: Chhote repo me ye sab karna — bina zaroorat ki complexity.

3. Clone fast karne ke tareeke

Har tareeka kab use karein — ek table me.

CheezDetail (Hinglish me)
git clone --depth 1Shallow clone — sirf latest commit, no history. CI ke liye best.
git clone --filter=blob:nonePartial clone — history lo, files on-demand lo.
Sparse checkoutSirf repo ka ek hissa checkout karo — monorepo ke liye.
git clone --single-branchSirf ek branch lo — baaki branches mat lo.
Normal clonePoora history — jab git log/blame chahiye ho.
# Normal clone — poora history (SLOW, bade repo me)
# git clone https://github.com/company/big-repo.git
# -> 10GB download, 10 minute!

# Shallow clone — sirf latest commit (FAST!)
# git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/company/big-repo.git
# -> 100MB download, 5 second! (99% kam!)
#
# CI me hamesha shallow clone use karo:
# GitHub Actions me default fetch-depth: 1 hota hai —
# isi liye CI fast hota hai!

GitHub Actions me default shallow clone hota hai (fetch-depth: 1) — isi liye CI me clone fast hota hai. Tumhare local clone me poora history aata hai.

4. Try karo — Clone time simulator

Ek bada repo clone karo — alag-alag tareeke se. Farak dekho.

5. Kab kya use karein

Option / SituationKab aur kyun
CI job haiShallow clone (--depth 1) — sirf latest code chahiye.
Naya developer, bas code chahiyeShallow clone — fast onboarding.
History bhi chahiye (git log)Normal clone ya partial clone.
Monorepo, ek project chahiyeSparse checkout — sirf apna hissa lo.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  • Har jagah shallow clone use karna — jahan history chahiye wahan nahi chalega.
  • Bina measure kiye optimize karna — pehle pata karo time kahan ja raha hai.
  • Bade repo ko normal clone karna — CI me hamesha shallow use karo.
  • Ye sochna ki network slow hai — aksar problem history ka size hoti hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: Pinterest ne clone time 99% kaise kam kiya?

Ek line badal ke — git clone me --depth 1 flag lagaya (shallow clone). Isse sirf latest commit download hota hai, poora history nahi. Repo ka 99% size history hi thi, to clone 99% fast ho gaya.

Q: Shallow clone kya hai aur kab use karna chahiye?

Shallow clone me sirf recent commits download hote hain (jaise --depth 1 me sirf latest). CI jobs aur fresh clones ke liye best hai — jahan history ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Jahan git log ya blame chahiye, wahan normal clone karo.

Q: Bade monorepo me clone fast karne ke aur kya tareeke hain?

Partial clone (--filter=blob:none) — files on-demand download karo. Sparse checkout — sirf repo ka ek hissa checkout karo. Single-branch clone — sirf ek branch lo. Har tareeka repo ka size kam karta hai.

8. Quick check

Q1. git clone --depth 1 ka matlab kya hai?

  • Poora history download karo
  • Sirf latest commit download karo — no history
  • Sirf ek file download karo

Q2. Clone me sabse zyada time kahan jata hai (bade repo me)?

  • Latest code download me
  • Poora history download me
  • Git install me

Original guide se — poori detail

Ye kahani Pinterest ki Engineering Productivity team ki hai. Unka monorepo Pinboard — Pinterest ka sabse purana aur sabse bada monorepo — clone karne me 40 minutes lagte the. Fix ke baad sirf 30 seconds — 99% kam.

  • Pinboard ke numbers: 350K commits; poora clone 20 GB; har business day 60K git pulls.
  • Pipeline: Jenkins build pipeline Groovy me likhi hai; "Checkout" stage me repo clone hota hai, phir build aur test steps chalte hain.
  • Pehle se kya tha: shallow clone on tha, tags fetch nahi hote the, sirf last 50 commits fetch hote the — phir bhi slow tha.
  • Asli wajah: Checkout step Git refspec option use nahi kar raha tha — har build pe saare refspecs fetch hote the, matlab 2500+ branches ka data.
  • Fix: refspec option add karke sirf "master" branch specify ki — ek line ka badlav, aur clone sirf ek branch se deal karta hai.

02Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Is Telegram Secure?

Telegram ke 900 million users hain — lekin kya wo secure hai? Jawab itna simple nahi hai: Telegram ke chats by default encrypted nahi hote, sirf Secret Chats hote hain. Aur uska encryption protocol (MTProto) experts ke beech controversial hai. Poori kahani samjho, phir decide karo.

1. Telegram secure hai? — chithhi wali kahani

Socho tum chithhi bhejte ho. Normal Telegram chat matlab chithhi ek lifafe me hai — postman (Telegram server) use khol ke padh sakta hai, phir dobara band karke bhej deta hai. Secret Chat matlab chithhi ek lock wale box me hai — sirf tum aur saamne wala khol sakte hain, postman bhi nahi. Signal/WhatsApp matlab har chithhi lock wale box me hai — by default. Telegram me lock wala box sirf tab milta hai jab tum khud maango (Secret Chat).

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Telegram ke normal chats server pe readable hote hain (cloud chats) — end-to-end encryption sirf Secret Chats me hai, aur wo by default ON nahi hai. Yehi sabse badi baat hai jo log nahi jante.

2. Telegram ki security — deep me

Har aspect ko samjho — encryption, protocol, aur trade-offs.

Cloud Chats vs Secret Chats

Cloud Chats (default): tumhare messages Telegram ke servers pe store hote hain — encrypted, lekin Telegram ke paas key hai. Matlab Telegram (aur jo use force kare) messages padh sakta hai. Fayda: kisi bhi device se access kar sakte ho, backup rehta hai. Secret Chats: end-to-end encrypted — sirf tum aur saamne wala padh sakte hain, Telegram bhi nahi. Lekin sirf ek device pe, no cloud backup, aur khud ON karna padta hai. Example: normal chat me tum phone aur laptop dono se padh sakte ho — kyunki messages server pe hain. Secret Chat sirf usi phone pe dikhega jahan shuru kiya.

Sahi tareeka: Sensitive baat ho to Secret Chat use karna.
Galat tareeka: Ye samajhna ki Telegram by default end-to-end encrypted hai — nahi hai!

MTProto — Telegram ka protocol

Telegram apna khud ka protocol use karta hai — MTProto. Signal aur WhatsApp Signal Protocol use karte hain — jo open-source hai aur experts ne bahut audit kiya hai. MTProto controversial hai — kuch experts kehte hain isme design issues hain, aur ye poori tarah open-source bhi nahi hai (server-side code closed hai). Example: 2021 me researchers ne MTProto me kuch flaws dikhaye — Telegram ne kuch fix kiye, kuch pe disagree kiya. Note: protocol ka audit hona bahut important hai — jo protocol zyada audit hua ho, wo zyada trustworthy hai.

Sahi tareeka: Security ke liye audit hua protocol (Signal Protocol) zyada safe hai.
Galat tareeka: MTProto ko Signal Protocol jitna trusted samajhna — audit kam hua hai.

Telegram vs Signal vs WhatsApp

Signal: by default end-to-end encrypted, open-source, sabse zyada trusted — lekin features kam hain. WhatsApp: by default end-to-end encrypted (Signal Protocol), lekin Meta ka hai — metadata (kaun kisse kab baat karta hai) Meta ko dikhta hai. Telegram: features sabse zyada (channels, bots, badi files), lekin by default E2E nahi hai. Example: privacy chahiye to Signal, features chahiye to Telegram, dono ka mix chahiye to WhatsApp. Note: koi app 100% secure nahi hoti — tumhari threat model pe depend karta hai (kisse chhupana hai?).

Sahi tareeka: Privacy chahiye to Signal, features chahiye to Telegram.
Galat tareeka: Ye samajhna ki Telegram WhatsApp jitna secure hai — default encryption me farak hai.

Metadata aur Privacy

Encryption ke alawa metadata bhi matter karta hai — kaun kisse kab baat karta hai, kitni der, kahan se. Telegram cloud chats me metadata bhi server pe hota hai. Example: tum kisiko message bhejte ho — Telegram ko pata hai tumne kisko, kab, kitna bada message bheja (content nahi, lekin metadata haan). Note: phone number se account banta hai — tumhara number hi pehchan hai. Tip: Telegram me username use karo, number chhupao; two-step verification ON karo; aur sensitive baat ke liye Secret Chat ya Signal use karo.

Sahi tareeka: Two-step verification ON karna + number chhupana.
Galat tareeka: Phone number public rakhna — koi bhi tumhe dhoondh sakta hai.

3. Telegram security — ek table me

Teeno apps ka comparison — kya secure hai, kya nahi.

CheezDetail (Hinglish me)
Default E2E encryptionTelegram: NAHI (sirf Secret Chats) | Signal: HAAN | WhatsApp: HAAN.
ProtocolTelegram: MTProto (controversial) | Signal: Signal Protocol (audited) | WhatsApp: Signal Protocol.
Open-sourceTelegram: client haan, server nahi | Signal: poora open | WhatsApp: nahi.
Cloud backupTelegram: haan (server pe readable) | Signal: nahi | WhatsApp: backup ho to readable.
FeaturesTelegram: sabse zyada | Signal: kam | WhatsApp: medium.
MetadataTelegram: server ko dikhta hai | Signal: kam se kam | WhatsApp: Meta ko dikhta hai.
# Telegram ko secure kaise use karein:
# 1. Two-step verification ON karo
#    (Settings > Privacy > Two-Step Verification)
# 2. Sensitive baat ke liye Secret Chat use karo
#    (New Secret Chat — E2E encrypted)
# 3. Phone number chhupao
#    (Settings > Privacy > Phone Number > Nobody)
# 4. Active sessions check karo
#    (Settings > Devices — unknown device ho to remove karo)
# 5. Passcode lock lagao
#    (Settings > Privacy > Passcode Lock)

Ye 5 steps 2 minute me kar sakte ho — aur Telegram ki security bahut badh jayegi. Secret Chat sabse important hai sensitive baaton ke liye.

4. Try karo — Telegram security simulator

Ek message bhejo — dekho kaun use padh sakta hai.

5. Kab kya use karein

Option / SituationKab aur kyun
Normal baat-cheet, groups, channelsTelegram normal chat — convenient hai, kaafi hai.
Sensitive baat hoTelegram Secret Chat ya Signal — E2E encryption chahiye.
Sabse zyada privacy chahiyeSignal — by default E2E, open-source, kam metadata.
Sabse zyada features chahiyeTelegram — channels, bots, badi files.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  • Ye samajhna ki Telegram by default end-to-end encrypted hai — sirf Secret Chats hain.
  • Secret Chat use kiye bina sensitive baat karna — normal chat server pe readable hai.
  • Two-step verification OFF rakhna — account hack ho jayega.
  • Phone number public rakhna — koi bhi tumhe dhoondh sakta hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: Telegram ke normal chats end-to-end encrypted hote hain?

Nahi — normal (cloud) chats me messages Telegram ke servers pe store hote hain. Wo encrypted hote hain, lekin key Telegram ke paas hai — matlab Telegram messages padh sakta hai. End-to-end encryption sirf Secret Chats me hai, jo by default ON nahi hota.

Q: MTProto kya hai aur controversial kyun hai?

MTProto Telegram ka khud ka encryption protocol hai. Controversial isliye hai kyunki ye Signal Protocol jitna audit nahi hua hai, server-side code open-source nahi hai, aur researchers ne isme kuch design issues dikhaye hain. Signal Protocol zyada trusted mana jata hai.

Q: Telegram, Signal aur WhatsApp me sabse secure kaunsa hai?

Signal sabse zyada trusted hai — by default E2E, open-source, kam metadata. WhatsApp bhi by default E2E hai (Signal Protocol) lekin Meta ka hai — metadata Meta ko dikhta hai. Telegram me features sabse zyada hain, lekin default E2E nahi hai.

8. Quick check

Q1. Telegram ke kaunse chats end-to-end encrypted hote hain?

  • Saare chats, by default
  • Sirf Secret Chats
  • Koi bhi nahi

Q2. Sabse zyada trusted (privacy ke liye) messaging app kaunsi hai?

  • Telegram
  • Signal
  • WhatsApp
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/is-telegram-secure.md

03Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

McDonald’s Event-Driven Architecture

McDonald’s sirf burger nahi bechta — uske peeche ek poora event-driven system chalta hai. Har order, har payment, har kitchen update ek event hai, aur ye events AWS par Kafka (MSK) se hote hue saare apps tak pahunchte hain. Samjho ye system kaise reliable rehta hai, jab ek bhi order kho jaaye to paise aur khana dono ka nuksaan hota hai.

1. McDonald’s ki kitchen — ek real-life analogy

McDonald’s ke restaurant ko ek shaadi ka khana samjho. Counter par order lene wala alag hai, burger banane wala alag, aur bill karne wala alag. Agar counter wala har baar kitchen me jaa ke chillaye — “ek Big Mac banao!” — to wo khud atak jayega, line ruk jayegi.

Isliye beech me ek order slip ka board hota hai: counter wala slip chipka deta hai aur turant agle customer ko attend karta hai. Kitchen apni speed se slip padhta hai aur burger banata hai. Slip hi event hai, board hi event broker (Kafka) hai, aur counter/kitchen hi producer/consumer hain.

Event-driven ka matlab: services ek dusre ko direct call nahi karti — wo events publish karti hain, aur jise chahiye wo subscribe karke sunta hai. Producer ko pata bhi nahi hota kaun sun raha hai. Isse system loosely coupled rehta hai: ek service down ho to bhi order slip board par safe rehti hai.

2. Event flow ke 5 main components

Diagram me McDonald’s ke 4 core components dikh rahe hain, plus Kafka aur standby store. Har tab me: ye kya karta hai, aur kharab hone pe kya hota hai.

Event Registry — events ka “dictionary”

Har event ka ek standard schema hota hai — jaise OrderPlaced me kya-kya fields honge: orderId, items, price, restaurantId. Event Registry ye schema define aur store karta hai, taaki har app same format bole.

Kyun zaroori hai? Bina registry ke ek app price bhejega, dusra amount — consumer confuse ho jayega. Registry versioning bhi karta hai: purana consumer purana schema padh sake, naya naya.

Sahi tareeka: schema change hamesha backward-compatible rakho — naya field optional banao, purana field kabhi rename mat karo.

Producer SDK — event bhejne ka safe tareeka

Har application me ek custom SDK hota hai jo event bhejne aur error handle karne ka kaam karta hai. App seedha Kafka ko call nahi karta — SDK se Send Event karta hai.

SDK pehle Schema Validation karta hai: schema match hua to event Primary topic me publish, nahi hua to DLQ (Dead-Letter Queue) me. Matlab galat format wala event system ko bigaadne ke bajay alag side me chala jata hai, jahan use baad me fix kiya ja sakta hai.

Galat hone pe: agar validation na ho to ek kharab event consumer ko crash kara dega, aur wo crash loop me hazaaron baar retry karega.

Event Gateway — pehredaar (authentication)

Event Gateway har event ko andar aane se pehle identity authentication aur authorization karta hai — kaun si app event bhej rahi hai, kya use is topic par publish karne ki permission hai?

Ye ek hi entry point hai, isliye security ek jagah enforce hoti hai. Bina gateway ke koi bhi app koi bhi event bhej sakti — galat ya nakli order events se poora system bhar jayega.

AWS MSK — events ki highway

Beech me hai AWS Managed Streaming for Kafka (MSK) — managed Kafka cluster. McDonald’s regional architecture use karta hai: har region me apna cluster, taaki global availability mile aur ek region down ho to dusra kaam kare.

Ek region ke andar events domain ke hisaab se shard hote hain — jaise orders alag, payments alag, inventory alag. Sharding se scale milta hai: zyada load ho to zyada partitions.

DLQ bhi MSK ke andar hi hai — galat events ke liye alag lane, taaki main lane kabhi block na ho.

Standby Event Store aur Admin Utility — jab Kafka hi down ho

Diagram ke neeche dekho: agar MSK Unavailable ho jaye, to events Standby Event Store me likhe jate hain — ek backup jagah, taaki ek bhi order na khoye. Kafka wapas aate hi Admin Utility un events ko dobara process karwata hai.

Retryable? Consumer ke paas ek diamond hai — event process nahi hua to poochta hai “retryable hai?” Haan to dobara try, nahi to Admin Utility ke paas bhej do. Isi ko reliable event processing kehte hain.

Interview line: “At-least-once delivery + idempotent consumer = practically no order loss.”

3. Poora flow — order se lekar kitchen tak

1. Customer app me order karta hai
   → App #1 (Producer SDK) event banata hai: OrderPlaced
2. SDK schema validate karta hai
   → OK  → Publish to Primary (MSK topic: orders)
   → FAIL → Publish to DLQ (baad me fix hoga)
3. Event Gateway: app ki identity + permission check
4. MSK topic me event store (replicated, durable)
5. Consumer (kitchen/inventory/billing) event padhta hai
   → Schema validate → Process Event
   → Fail? Retryable hai to retry, nahi to Admin Utility
6. MSK down? → Standby Event Store me likho, baad me replay

Regional sharding ka fayda: US ke orders US region me, Europe ke Europe me — latency kam, aur ek region ki problem dusre ko nahi chhooti. Global availability ka yehi matlab hai.

4. Try karo — ek order event ki journey

Button dabao aur dekho ek McDonald’s order event system ke andar kya-kya karta hai.

5. Components — ek table me

ComponentKaamNa ho to kya hoga
Event RegistryHar event ka schema define karta haiHar app alag format bolega — consumer toot jayega
Producer SDKEvent bhejna + validation + error handlingKharab events seedha Kafka me, consumer crash loop
Event GatewayAuthentication + authorizationKoi bhi nakli event bhej dega — security khatam
AWS MSK (Kafka)Events store + distribute karta haiServices ko direct call karna padega — tight coupling
DLQGalat events ko side me rakhta haiEk kharab event poori pipeline rok dega
Standby Event StoreKafka down ho to events bachata haiDowntime me saare orders kho jayenge

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Schema bina version ke badal dena — purane consumers ke liye event unreadable ho jata hai; hamesha backward-compatible change karo. 2. DLQ ko kabhi na dekhna — DLQ dustbin nahi hai; usme pade events ka matlab hai real bug, use monitor + replay karo. 3. Producer me retry bina idempotency ke — retry se duplicate orders ban jayenge; consumer idempotent banao. 4. Event Gateway ke bina seedha Kafka expose karna — koi bhi app kuch bhi publish kar dega. 5. Standby store ka failover kabhi test na karna — asli outage me pata chalega ki replay kaam hi nahi karta; game day karo.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. McDonald’s me galat schema wala event kahan jata hai?

  • DLQ (Dead-Letter Queue) me — main pipeline block nahi hoti — sahi jawab ✓
  • Seedha delete ho jata hai
  • Consumer ko crash kar deta hai

2. MSK (Kafka) down ho jaye to order events ka kya hota hai?

  • Standby Event Store me likhe jate hain, baad me replay hote hain — sahi jawab ✓
  • Hamesha ke liye kho jate hain
  • Customer ko dobara order karna padta hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Events ek standard schema se publish hote hain, Kafka unhe reliably deliver karta hai, galat events DLQ me jate hain aur Kafka down ho to standby store order bachata hai — isiliye McDonald’s ka ek bhi order nahi kho sakta.

Original guide se — poori detail

McDonald's events ko standardize karne ke liye 4 components use karta hai:

  • Event Registry: standardized schema define karta hai.
  • Custom SDKs: events process karne aur errors handle karne ke liye custom software development kits.
  • Event Gateway: identity authentication aur authorization karta hai.
  • Utilities and Tools: events fix karna, cluster healthy rakhna aur administrative tasks.

Scaling: regional architecture AWS par global availability deti hai. Har region me producers events ko domain ke hisaab se shard karte hain; har domain ko ek MSK cluster process karta hai. Cluster MSK metrics (jaise CPU usage) ke basis par auto-scale karta hai; auto-scale workflow step-functions aur re-assignment tasks par based hai.

04Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Uber Tech Stack - CI/CD

Uber roz hazaaron engineers ka code production me daalta hai — bina service roke, bina rider ko pata chale. Iske peeche ek CI/CD pipeline hai jo planning se lekar deploy tak har step ko automate karta hai, aur Uber ne iske liye apne tools bhi banaye hain: NullAway, Piranha, Flipr aur Bazel. Dekhte hain ye machine kaise chalti hai.

1. CI/CD kya hai? — dhaba wali kahani

Ek dhabe ko samjho: roz naya menu item aata hai. Agar cook seedha customer ko bina taste kiye de de, to kabhi namak zyada, kabhi kachha. Achha dhaba ek chakne wala system rakhta hai — pehle chhota sa taste, phir 2-3 customers ko try karwao, phir sabko do.

CI/CD wahi hai: CI (Continuous Integration) = har code change ko turant build + test karo; CD (Continuous Deployment) = test pass ho to dheere-dheere sab users tak pahunchao. Uber par ye roz hazaaron baar hota hai.

2. Uber ki CI/CD pipeline ke 5 hisse

Guide ke hisaab se Uber ki pipeline ke main tools aur steps — har tab me ek stage.

Planning — JIRA

Kaam JIRA me plan hota hai: ticket, sprint, priority. Bada feature chhote tickets me tootta hai, taaki har ticket ek deployable change bane.

Kyun zaroori hai? Bina planning ke CI/CD sirf tez tareeka hai galat cheez deploy karne ka. JIRA se har deploy ka “kyun” pata chalta hai — kaun sa ticket, kis liye.

Code quality — Uber ke apne tools

NullAway — NullPointerException pakadta hai compile time par, production me crash hone se pehle. NEAL — code lint karta hai, style aur common galtiyan pakadta hai.

Piranha — purane feature flags ko saaf karta hai. Feature flag ek switch hota hai jo feature on/off karta hai; purane flags code me reh jayein to code ganda aur risky ho jata hai. Piranha unhe automatically hata deta hai.

Sahi tareeka: quality checks CI me daalo — developer ke local machine par nahi, pipeline me — taaki koi bhi kharab code aage na badhe.

Monorepo + Bazel — ek repo, tez build

Uber Monorepo use karta hai — saara code ek hi repository me. Isse code share karna aur dependency manage karna aasan hota hai.

Build ke liye Bazel hai — Google ka build tool. Bazel sirf wahi cheez dobara build karta hai jo badli hai (incremental build), isliye lakhon lines wale repo me bhi build tez rehta hai. Bina iske har chhota change ghanton ka build ban jata.

Flipr — bina deploy ke config badlo

Flipr Uber ka configuration system hai. Isse config changes (jaise koi limit 100 se 200 karna) bina code deploy ke turant release hote hain.

Kyun badi baat hai? Agar har chhoti setting ke liye poora deploy karna pade, to ek galti fix karne me ghanta lag jayega. Flipr se config seconds me badalta hai — aur galat ho to turant wapas bhi.

Deploy — ek saath sabko nahi, dheere-dheere

Uber ek saath saare servers par naya code nahi daalta. Pehle 1% traffic, phir 10%, phir 100% — gradual / canary rollout. Agar naye code me bug ho, to sirf 1% users ko farak padega aur rollback turant ho jayega.

Feature flags ke saath deploy aur release alag ho jate hain: code production me hai, lekin feature off hai — jab chaho tab on karo, bina deploy ke.

Galat hone pe: “big bang” deploy — ek saath sab kuch — ek bug se poori service down. Uber jaisi scale par ye kabhi nahi karna.

3. Pipeline ka flow — commit se production tak

Developer code likhta hai → Pull Request
  1. CI trigger: Bazel build (sirf badla hua hissa)
  2. NullAway: null-safety check (compile time)
  3. NEAL: lint + style check
  4. Unit + integration tests chalte hain
  5. Piranha: purane feature flags saaf
  6. Review + merge → Monorepo (main branch)
  7. CD: canary deploy — 1% → 10% → 100% traffic
  8. Flipr: config change bina deploy ke
  9. Monitoring: error rate badha? → auto rollback

Monorepo ka trade-off: code sharing aasan, lekin repo bada — isliye Bazel jaisa smart build tool zaroori hai. Chhoti team ke liye polyrepo bhi theek hai; tool scale ke hisaab se chuno, hype ke hisaab se nahi.

4. Try karo — ek code change ki journey

Button dabao aur dekho ek developer ka chhota sa change Uber ki pipeline se kaise guzarta hai.

5. Tools — ek table me

Tool / StepKaamFayda
JIRAPlanning aur ticketsHar deploy ka reason track hota hai
NullAwayNullPointer compile time par pakadta haiProduction crash kam hote hain
NEALLint + code styleCodebase ek jaisa aur readable rehta hai
PiranhaPurane feature flags saaf karta haiDead code aur risk kam hota hai
Bazel + MonorepoIncremental build, ek repoBade repo me bhi build tez rehta hai
FliprBina deploy ke config releaseSetting badlo seconds me, rollback bhi seconds me
Canary deploy1% → 100% gradual rolloutBug ho to sirf 1% users affected, rollback tez

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Tests ke bina seedha production deploy — CI ka matlab hi hai har change test ho; test skip karna matlab andhere me deploy. 2. Big-bang deploy karna — ek saath 100% traffic par naya code; canary rollout skip mat karo. 3. Feature flags ko kabhi saaf na karna — saal bhar purane flags code ko unreadable aur risky bana dete hain; Piranha jaisa cleanup rakho. 4. Config change ke liye bhi full deploy — config aur code ko alag rakho (Flipr jaisa system). 5. Rollback plan ke bina deploy — agar error rate badhe to wapas jaane ka button pehle se ready hona chahiye.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Uber me NullAway kis liye hai?

  • NullPointerException ko compile time par pakadne ke liye — sahi jawab ✓
  • Code ko fast chalane ke liye
  • Feature flags saaf karne ke liye

2. Flipr ka sabse bada fayda kya hai?

  • Config change bina code deploy ke turant release hoti hai — sahi jawab ✓
  • Ye ek database hai
  • Ye code ko test karta hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Har change pehle build + test hota hai (CI), phir canary rollout se dheere-dheere production me jata hai (CD) — aur config Flipr se bina deploy ke badalti hai. Isiliye Uber roz hazaaron deploy bina downtime ke karta hai.

Original guide se — poori detail

Uber ke CI/CD tech stack ki poori list (guide se):

  • Project planning: JIRA.
  • Backend services: Spring Boot; fast config releases ke liye Flipr naam ka configuration system.
  • Code issues: NullAway (NullPointer problems), NEAL (code lint), Piranha (outdated feature flags saaf karna).
  • Repository: Monorepo; bade scale par Bazel.
  • Testing: SLATE (short-lived testing environments), Shadower (production traffic replay karke load testing), Ballast (smooth user experience ensure karna).
  • Experiment platform: deep learning par based; Pyro open-source kiya gaya hai.
  • Build: uBuild se services containers me package hoti hain; Buildkite se powered hai.
  • Deploying: Netflix Spinnaker — production me smoothly deploy karne ke liye.
  • Monitoring: khud ka monitoring system; uMetric platform Cassandra par bana hai.
  • Special tooling: Peloton (capacity planning, scheduling, operations), Crane (multi-cloud infrastructure, cost optimize), uAct aur OnCall dashboard (event tracing aur on-call duty management).
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/uber-tech-stack-cicd.md

05Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

How to Design Stack Overflow

Interview me Stack Overflow design poochha jaye to zyada log microservices, sharding aur event sourcing ki lambi list suna dete hain. Lekin asli Stack Overflow sirf 9 on-premise servers aur ek monolith par chalta hai! Ye page batata hai — interviewer kya sunna chahta hai, aur reality me kya kaam karta hai.

1. Interview vs Reality — do alag duniya

Interview me tumse expect karte hain: microservices, har service ka apna database, cache, sharding, message queue, event sourcing + CQRS, CAP theorem ki baatein. Ye sab “impressive” lagta hai.

Reality: Stack Overflow apna saara traffic sirf 9 on-premise servers se serve karta hai — monolith + SQL Server. Kyunki unka traffic pattern read-heavy hai, data zyada badalta nahi, aur simple architecture hi unke liye fastest aur cheapest hai.

Interview ka asli lesson: interviewer tumhari “buzzword list” nahi, tumhari soch dekhna chahta hai — requirements samjho, trade-off batao, aur simple solution ko justify karo. “Sab kuch microservices me tod do” galat jawab bhi ho sakta hai.

2. Design ke 5 main hisse

Pehle interview wala design, phir asli design — dono ko samjho, tabhi interview me achha jawab de paoge.

Interviewer kya expect karta hai?

Microservices me todna, har service ka apna database, cache heavily use karna, services ko shard karna, services ke beech async communication (message queues), event sourcing + CQRS, aur eventual consistency / CAP theorem ki baatein.

Ye galat nahi hai — ye ek valid design hai, khaas taur par agar scale bahut zyada ho. Lekin interviewer ye bhi dekhna chahta hai ki tum kyun ye choose kar rahe ho, sirf kya nahi.

Asliyat — monolith hi kaafi hai

Stack Overflow ek monolith hai: saara code ek hi application me. Deploy simple, debugging simple, aur ek request ke liye service-to-service network calls nahi — sab in-process hai, isliye latency bahut kam hai.

Kab monolith sahi hai? Jab team chhoti ho, domain simple ho, aur traffic ek machine ke capacity me aa jaye. Microservices ka overhead (network, deployment, debugging) tabhi justify hota hai jab scale ya team size uski demand kare.

Database — SQL Server, sharding nahi

Stack Overflow SQL Server use karta hai — ek hi powerful database, bina sharding ke. Questions, answers, votes — sab relational data hai, joins chahiye, isliye SQL natural fit hai.

Scale kaise? Read-heavy workload hai — zyada log padhte hain, kam likhte hain. Isliye read replicas aur aggressive caching se kaam chal jata hai; har cheez ko shard karne ki zaroorat nahi padti.

Caching — asli hero

Stack Overflow ki speed ka raaz caching hai: popular questions, tags, user profiles — sab cache me. Ek question ek baar render ho to hazaaron baar cache se serve hota hai.

Cache invalidation yahan aasan hai kyunki writes kam hain: naya answer aaye to sirf us question ka cache clear karo. Read-heavy + kam writes = caching ka best case.

Sahi tareeka: pehle cache aur read replica try karo; sharding tab karo jab data ek machine me na aaye.

On-premise servers — cloud kyun nahi?

Stack Overflow apne khud ke servers (on-premise) chalata hai, cloud par nahi. Unke hisaab se unka load predictable hai, aur apne hardware par chalana unhe sasta aur control me lagta hai.

Lesson: har system ko cloud ki zaroorat nahi. Cost, control aur predictable load ho to on-premise bhi sahi decision hai. Interview me “cloud use karenge” default jawab nahi hona chahiye — trade-off batao.

3. Interview me kaise jawab do — structure

1. Requirements poochho (clarify karo)
   - Kitne users? Read-heavy ya write-heavy?
   - Question/answer/vote/search — kaun se features?
2. Scale estimate karo
   - Stack Overflow: ~100M monthly users, lekin
     writes bahut kam (sawaal poochhne wale kam, padhne wale zyada)
3. High-level design
   - Load balancer → Web servers (monolith) → SQL Server
   - Cache layer (Redis) + CDN static assets ke liye
   - Search ke liye alag service (Elasticsearch)
4. Deep dive: kahan scale karna hai
   - Read replicas, caching, DB indexing
   - Hot questions ka cache, vote counting async
5. Trade-offs bolo
   - “Main monolith se shuru karunga, kyunki...”
   - “Microservices tab, jab team/scale badhe”

Search ka note: full-text search ke liye SQL LIKE slow hai — isliye Elasticsearch jaisa alag search engine use hota hai. Ye ek valid jagah hai jahan alag service justify hoti hai.

4. Try karo — ek question ki journey

Button dabao aur dekho ek Stack Overflow question system ke andar kaise travel karta hai.

5. Interview design vs Real design

CheezInterview me expect karte hainAsli Stack Overflow
ArchitectureMicroservicesMonolith
ServersCloud, auto-scaling, hazaaron nodes9 on-premise servers
DatabaseHar service ka apna DB, shardingEk SQL Server + read replicas
CommunicationMessage queues, event sourcing, CQRSIn-process calls + thoda async
Scaling ka raazSharding + distributed systemsAggressive caching

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Har system ko microservices me todna — bina scale/team reason ke microservices sirf complexity badhate hain. 2. Requirements poochhe bina design shuru karna — read-heavy hai ya write-heavy, ye jaane bina sahi design nahi ban sakta. 3. Sharding ko pehla solution banana — pehle cache, indexing aur read replica try karo. 4. Buzzwords ki list sunana bina trade-off ke — interviewer ko ‘kyun’ chahiye, ‘kya’ nahi. 5. Search ke liye SQL LIKE use karna — full-text search ke liye Elasticsearch jaisa engine chahiye.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Asli Stack Overflow apna traffic kitne servers par serve karta hai?

  • Sirf 9 on-premise servers par — sahi jawab ✓
  • 1000+ cloud servers par
  • 500 microservices par

2. Stack Overflow jaisi read-heavy site me scaling ka sabse pehla aur best step kya hai?

  • Aggressive caching + read replicas — sahi jawab ✓
  • Database ko 100 shards me todna
  • Har feature ko alag microservice banana
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Interview me design hamesha requirements aur trade-offs se shuru karo — Stack Overflow iska sabse achha example hai: simple monolith + SQL Server + caching, bina microservices ke, karodon users serve karta hai.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-will-you-design-the-stack-overflow-website.md
← PichhlaUber Tech Stack - CI/CDAgla →Twitter 1.0 Tech Stack
06Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Twitter 1.0 Tech Stack

Twitter 1.0 — wo zamana jab Twitter ne apni pehchan banayi. Uske peeche ka tech stack aaj ke hisaab se simple lagta hai, lekin usi par karodon tweets chalte the. Mobile se lekar database tak — poora stack ek table me samjho.

1. Twitter 1.0 ko samjho — ek newspaper ki kahani

Twitter ko ek sheher ka newspaper samjho: roz lakhon log khabar bhej rahe hain (tweets), aur karodon log padh rahe hain. Newspaper ko chahiye: tez printing (write), tez delivery (read), aur purani khabron ka archive (storage).

Twitter 1.0 ne har kaam ke liye alag tool chuna: likhne ke liye alag, padhne ke liye cache, aur store karne ke liye alag-alag databases. Ek tool sab kuch nahi karta — har problem ka sahi tool yehi us stack ki khaasiyat hai.

2. Stack ki 5 paratein (layers)

Guide ke hisaab se Twitter 1.0 ki har layer — kya use hota tha, aur kyun.

Mobile — Swift, Kotlin, PWA

iOS app Swift me, Android app Kotlin me — native apps, taaki scrolling aur animations smooth rahen. Saath me PWA (Progressive Web App) bhi — halke internet par bhi Twitter chal sake.

Kyun native? Timeline scroll karte waqt 60fps chahiye hota hai; web view me wo smoothness mushkil hai. Native se push notifications aur offline bhi aasan hota hai.

Web — JavaScript, React, Redux

Website React se bani hai, state ke liye Redux. Timeline ek live feed hai — naya tweet aate hi UI update hona chahiye, bina page reload ke.

Redux ka kaam: poori app ka state ek jagah rakhna — kaun se tweets dikhe, kaun sa like hua, notifications kya hain. Bina iske har component apna state rakhta aur UI inconsistent ho jata.

Services — Mesos, Finagle

Backend services Finagle (Twitter ka RPC framework) se baat karti hain — Scala/Java based, high-throughput service-to-service calls ke liye bana hai.

Mesos cluster manager hai — hazaaron machines par services ko schedule karta hai: kaun si service kis machine par chalegi, kitne instances chahiye. Aaj iski jagah Kubernetes ne le li hai, lekin concept wahi hai.

Caching — Pelikan Cache, Redis

Pelikan Cache Twitter ka apna cache hai (Memcached ka successor) — timelines aur hot tweets ko memory me rakhta hai, taaki har request DB tak na jaye.

Redis bhi use hota hai — counters (likes, retweets), timelines, aur rate limiting ke liye. Cache ke bina har timeline request database ko maregi aur Twitter ruk jayega.

Databases — Manhattan, MySQL, PostgreSQL

Manhattan Twitter ka apna distributed key-value store hai — tweets aur timelines ka main store, jo scale ke liye bana hai.

MySQL aur PostgreSQL relational kaam ke liye — jahan joins aur transactions chahiye, jaise user accounts aur billing. Ek database sab kuch nahi karta — har data ki nature ke hisaab se alag store.

Interview line: “Polyglot persistence — har data ke liye sahi database, ek database se sab kuch karne ki zidd nahi.”

3. Ek tweet ki journey — likhne se dikhne tak

1. User tweet likhta hai (Swift/Kotlin app ya React web)
2. Request Finagle service tak jati hai
3. Tweet Manhattan (key-value store) me save hota hai
4. MySQL/PostgreSQL me user ka metadata update hota hai
5. Followers ki timelines Pelikan/Redis cache me update hoti hain
   (fan-out: ek tweet → lakhon followers ki timeline)
6. Dusre users ko timeline cache se milti hai — DB touch nahi hota

Fan-out problem: ek celebrity ke 10 crore followers hain — uska ek tweet 10 crore timelines me daalna padta hai. Isliye Twitter “fan-out on write” aur “fan-out on read” dono ka mix use karta hai (ye Page 61 me detail me hai).

4. Try karo — ek tweet post karo

Button dabao aur dekho ek tweet Twitter 1.0 ke stack se kaise guzarta hai.

5. Layer — ek table me

LayerTechKyun yehi
MobileSwift, Kotlin, PWANative smoothness + halke net par PWA
WebJavaScript, React, ReduxLive timeline, ek jagah state
ServicesMesos, FinagleHigh-throughput RPC + cluster scheduling
CachingPelikan Cache, RedisTimeline aur counters memory se — DB bachta hai
DatabasesManhattan, MySQL, PostgreSQLScale ke liye KV store, relations ke liye SQL

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Ek hi database se sab kuch karna — tweets, relations, counters — har data ki alag nature hoti hai; polyglot persistence samjho. 2. Cache ko optional samajhna — Twitter jaisi read-heavy system me cache ke bina DB pehle din hi gir jayega. 3. Fan-out ko ignore karna — celebrity ka tweet lakhon timelines me jata hai; ye design ka sabse mushkil hissa hai. 4. Web ko native jaisa smooth samajhna — timeline scrolling ke liye native performance aur state management (Redux) chahiye. 5. Mesos/Kubernetes ko sirf ‘deployment tool’ samajhna — ye cluster scheduling hai: kaun si service kahan chalegi, kitne instances — ye capacity planning hai.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Twitter 1.0 me tweets ka main store kaun sa tha?

  • Manhattan — Twitter ka apna distributed key-value store — sahi jawab ✓
  • MySQL
  • Redis

2. Twitter me Pelikan Cache ka kaam kya hai?

  • Timelines aur hot data ko memory me rakhna taaki DB na mare — sahi jawab ✓
  • Tweets ko permanently store karna
  • Mobile app chalana
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Har layer ka apna tool — native mobile, React web, Finagle services, Pelikan/Redis cache aur Manhattan + SQL databases. Ek tool se sab kuch karne ki koshish hi sabse badi galti hoti hai.

← PichhlaHow to Design Stack OverflowAgla →Netflix Tech Stack - Databases
07Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Netflix Tech Stack - Databases

Netflix ek database nahi, kai databases use karta hai — billing ke liye MySQL, global transactions ke liye CockroachDB, analytics ke liye Redshift/Druid, aur caching ke liye EVCache. Har data ki nature alag hai, to database bhi alag. Yehi polyglot persistence hai.

1. Databases — kitchen ke bartan wali kahani

Ek kitchen me ek hi bartan se sab kuch nahi banta — chai ke liye kettle, roti ke liye tawa, biryani ke liye handi. Har kaam ka sahi bartan hota hai.

Netflix ke databases wahi hain: paise ka hisaab (billing) ke liye strong consistency wala SQL, video dekhne ka data ke liye tez key-value store, aur analytics ke liye columnar database. Ek database se sab kuch karne ki koshish karna matlab tawa me chai banana.

2. Netflix ke databases — 5 categories

Guide ke hisaab se — har category me kaun sa database, aur kis kaam ke liye.

Relational — MySQL aur CockroachDB

MySQL — billing transactions, subscriptions, taxes aur revenue ke liye. Paise ka mamla hai — ACID transactions aur strong consistency chahiye, isliye relational DB.

CockroachDB — multi-region active-active architecture, global transactions aur data pipeline workflows ke liye. Duniya bhar ke regions me ek hi logical database — likho kahin bhi, padho kahin bhi.

Columnar — Redshift aur Druid (analytics)

Analytics ke liye columnar databases: Redshift aur Druid structured data ke liye, Spark data pipeline processing ke liye, aur Tableau visualization ke liye.

Columnar ka matlab: data columns ke hisaab se store hota hai — “saare users ki average watch time” jaisi query par sirf ek column padhna padta hai, poori row nahi. Analytics queries isiliye tez hoti hain.

Key-Value — EVCache (Memcached par bana)

EVCache Netflix ka distributed key-value store hai, Memcached par bana hua, 10+ saal se use me. Most services use karti hain — caching, session, homepage data (Page 64 me detail hai).

Key-value ka matlab: key do, value lo — milliseconds me. Joins ya complex queries nahi, sirf tez lookups.

Wide-column — Cassandra

Cassandra — high write throughput aur massive scale ke liye. Jaise viewing history, user activity — karodon writes roz, aur reads bhi distributed.

Cassandra ka design: likhna bahut tez, aur node add karke scale karo. Lekin joins nahi — data ko query ke hisaab se pehle se design karna padta hai (query-first modelling).

Interview line: “Cassandra me pehle query likho, phir table banao — SQL ki tarah table pehle bana ke query nahi sochte.”

Baaki stores — har kaam ka alag tool

Netflix aur bhi specialized stores use karta hai — jaise search ke liye Elasticsearch jaisa engine, aur time-series metrics ke liye alag store. Har store ka ek kaam hai.

Lesson: “Kaun sa database best hai?” ka jawab hamesha hota hai — “kis kaam ke liye?” Paise ke liye MySQL, scale ke liye Cassandra, analytics ke liye Redshift, speed ke liye EVCache.

3. Kaun sa data, kaun sa database

DataDatabaseKyun
Billing, subscription, taxMySQLACID, strong consistency — paise me galti nahi chalegi
Global transactions, multi-regionCockroachDBActive-active, duniya bhar me ek logical DB
Analytics, reportingRedshift, Druid + SparkColumnar — badi queries tez
Cache, sessions, homepageEVCache (Memcached)Milliseconds me key-value lookup
Viewing history, high writesCassandraWrite throughput + horizontal scale
VisualizationTableauDashboards aur reports

4. Try karo — ek user ki journey, har database se

Button dabao aur dekho Netflix ke alag-alag databases ek user ke liye kaise kaam karte hain.

5. Database types — ek table me

TypeExampleBest for
Relational (SQL)MySQL, CockroachDBPaise, transactions, strong consistency
ColumnarRedshift, DruidAnalytics, badi aggregate queries
Key-ValueEVCacheCache, sessions, tez lookups
Wide-columnCassandraMassive writes, horizontal scale
SearchElasticsearchFull-text search

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Ek database se sab kuch karna — billing bhi aur analytics bhi; har workload ki alag zaroorat hoti hai. 2. Paise wale data ko eventually consistent store me rakhna — billing me strong consistency chahiye. 3. Cassandra me SQL jaisi soch — joins ki ummeed karna; Cassandra me query-first design hota hai. 4. Analytics queries ko main (OLTP) database par chalana — reporting se production slow ho jayega; alag columnar store use karo. 5. Cache ko database samajhna — EVCache tez hai lekin durable store nahi; critical data ka source of truth alag rakho.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Netflix billing (paise) ke liye kaun sa database use karta hai?

  • MySQL — ACID aur strong consistency ke liye — sahi jawab ✓
  • Cassandra
  • EVCache

2. Analytics queries ke liye columnar database kyun behtar hai?

  • Sirf zaroori columns padhne padte hain, poori row nahi — badi queries tez hoti hain — sahi jawab ✓
  • Isme zyada data store hota hai
  • Ye free hota hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Billing MySQL, global transactions CockroachDB, analytics Redshift/Druid, cache EVCache, massive writes Cassandra. Har data ki nature ke hisaab se database chuno — ‘best database’ naam ki koi cheez nahi hoti.

Original guide se — poori detail

Netflix har kaam ke liye alag database chunta hai:

  • Relational: MySQL — billing transactions, subscriptions, taxes, revenue. CockroachDB — multi-region active-active architecture, global transactions, data pipeline workflows.
  • Columnar (analytics): Redshift aur Druid (structured data storage), Spark (data pipeline processing), Tableau (data visualization).
  • Key-value: EVCache (Memcached par bana) — 10 saal se zyada se use me hai; Netflix Homepage aur Personal Recommendations jaisa data cache karta hai.
  • Wide-column: Cassandra default choice — Video/Actor information, User Data, Device information, Viewing History.
  • Time-series: Atlas — Netflix ka open-source in-memory database, metrics storage aur aggregation ke liye.
  • Unstructured: S3 default choice — Image/Video/Metrics/Log files. Apache Iceberg S3 ke saath big data storage ke liye.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/netflix-tech-stack-databases.md
← PichhlaTwitter 1.0 Tech StackAgla →Netflix's Overall Architecture
08Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Netflix's Overall Architecture

Netflix ka poora architecture ek page me: mobile se lekar video storage tak. Swift/Kotlin apps, React web, GraphQL, Zuul + Eureka + Spring Boot backend, EVCache + Cassandra + CockroachDB, Kafka + Flink streaming, aur video ke liye S3 + Open Connect. Ye page poora map hai.

1. Netflix ko samjho — ek sheher wali kahani

Netflix ek poora sheher hai: ghar (mobile/web apps), sadkein (GraphQL + API gateway), bijli ghar (backend services), godown (databases), aur delivery trucks (CDN + Open Connect). Har hisse ka apna kaam hai, aur sab ek dusre se jude hain.

Is page ka kaam hai poora map dikhana — taaki jab koi poochhe “Netflix kaise kaam karta hai?”, to tum ek saans me har layer bata sako.

2. Architecture ki 6 paratein

Guide ke hisaab se — har layer me kya use hota hai.

Mobile aur Web — Swift, Kotlin, React

Mobile apps native hain: iOS Swift me, Android Kotlin me — smooth scrolling aur video playback ke liye. Web app React se bani hai.

Native apps isliye kyunki video player, downloads aur background playback ko OS ke saath gehra integration chahiye hota hai — web view se wo nahi milta.

Frontend aur server ke beech — GraphQL

Frontend aur server GraphQL se baat karte hain. REST me har screen ke liye kai API calls lagti hain; GraphQL me frontend ek hi query me wahi data maangta hai jo use chahiye — na zyada, na kam.

Mobile ko chhota data, TV ko bada — GraphQL se har client apni zaroorat ke hisaab se maang sakta hai, backend ko har client ke liye alag API nahi banana padta.

Backend — Zuul, Eureka, Spring Boot

Backend microservices hain, Java + Spring Boot par. Zuul API gateway hai — saari requests pehle Zuul se guzarti hain (routing, auth, rate limiting). Eureka service discovery hai — kaun si service kahan chal rahi hai, ye Eureka batata hai.

Gateway + discovery ke bina hazaaron services ko dhoondhna aur call karna namumkin hota.

Databases — EVCache, Cassandra, CockroachDB

EVCache — tez key-value cache (Page 64-65 me detail). Cassandra — massive writes, jaise viewing history. CockroachDB — multi-region global transactions. Har data ke liye sahi store — polyglot persistence.

Messaging aur Streaming — Kafka aur Flink

Services ke beech events Apache Kafka se jate hain, aur real-time processing Flink se hoti hai — jaise abhi kitne log kya dekh rahe hain, recommendations update karna.

Kafka events ka backbone hai: ek service event publish karti hai, kai services sunti hain — bina ek dusre ko jaane.

Video storage — S3 aur Open Connect

Videos S3 (object storage) me store hote hain, aur delivery ke liye Netflix ka apna CDN hai — Open Connect. Netflix apne servers (Open Connect Appliances) ISPs ke andar hi lagata hai, taaki video tumhare ghar ke paas se aaye.

Isiliye Netflix itna tez hai — video kisi door ke data center se nahi, tumhare sheher ke ISP se aata hai.

Interview line: “Open Connect Netflix ka sabse bada competitive advantage hai — content ko user ke jitna paas ho sake, utna paas rakho.”

3. Ek request ki journey — play dabane se video chalne tak

1. Tum app me "Play" dabate ho (Swift/Kotlin ya React)
2. GraphQL query: video ka metadata + stream URL chahiye
3. Zuul gateway → Eureka se service dhoondhta hai
4. Playback service: EVCache check (session + metadata)
5. Cassandra: viewing history me write (tumne ye dekha)
6. Kafka event: "user started watching" → Flink → recommendations
7. Video: Open Connect (tumhare ISP ke paas wala server) se stream
8. Player adaptive bitrate se quality adjust karta hai

4. Try karo — Play dabao

Button dabao aur dekho Play dabate hi Netflix ke andar kya-kya hota hai.

5. Poora stack — ek table me

LayerTechKaam
MobileSwift, KotlinNative apps — smooth playback
WebReactWeb app
APIGraphQLFrontend apni zaroorat ka data maange
Gateway + DiscoveryZuul, EurekaRouting, auth, service dhoondhna
BackendSpring Boot (Java)Microservices
DatabasesEVCache, Cassandra, CockroachDBCache, writes, global transactions
StreamingKafka, FlinkEvents + real-time processing
VideoS3 + Open ConnectStorage + ISP ke paas se delivery

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Poora stack ek hi technology se banana — har layer ki alag zaroorat hoti hai. 2. Gateway ke bina microservices expose karna — client ko hazaaron services ka pata chal jayega. 3. Service discovery bhoolna — services ke IP badalte rehte hain; Eureka jaisa system chahiye. 4. Video ko normal server se serve karna — video ke liye CDN/Open Connect jaisa edge delivery chahiye. 5. REST se har client ko ek jaisa data dena — mobile aur TV ki zaroorat alag hai; GraphQL se har client apna data maange.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Netflix me API gateway kaun sa hai?

  • Zuul — sahi jawab ✓
  • Eureka
  • Flink

2. Netflix videos deliver karne ke liye kya use karta hai?

  • Open Connect — apna CDN, ISPs ke andar servers — sahi jawab ✓
  • Sirf S3 se seedha
  • YouTube se
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Swift/Kotlin apps + React web, GraphQL API, Zuul gateway + Eureka discovery, Spring Boot microservices, EVCache/Cassandra/CockroachDB, Kafka/Flink, aur S3 + Open Connect se video delivery. Har layer ka apna tool — poora map yaad rakho.

Original guide se — poori detail

Netflix ke tech stack ki poori list (guide se):

  • Mobile aur web: Swift aur Kotlin (native mobile apps), React (web application).
  • Frontend/server communication: GraphQL.
  • Backend services: ZUUL, Eureka, Spring Boot framework.
  • Databases: EVCache, Cassandra, CockroachDB.
  • Messaging/streaming: Apache Kafka aur Flink (guide me "Fink" likha hai — ye Flink hi hai).
  • Video storage: S3 aur Open Connect.
  • Data processing: Flink aur Spark; visualization Tableau se; structured data warehouse ke liye Redshift.
  • CI/CD: JIRA, Confluence, PagerDuty, Jenkins, Gradle, Chaos Monkey, Spinnaker, Atlas.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/netflixs-overall-architecture.md
← PichhlaNetflix Tech Stack - DatabasesAgla →Netflix Tech Stack - CI/CD Pipeline
09Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Netflix Tech Stack - CI/CD Pipeline

Netflix roz hazaaron baar deploy karta hai — bina tumhe pata chale, bina stream ruke. Uske peeche ek CI/CD pipeline hai: JIRA se planning, Gradle se build, Spinnaker se canary deploy, aur chaos tools se testing. Dekhte hain ye pipeline kaise chalti hai.

1. CI/CD pipeline — film shooting wali kahani

Film shooting me pehle script (planning), phir shooting (coding), phir editing (build), phir test screening (testing), phir dheere-dheere theatres me release (deploy). Agar test screening me film kharab lage to poori duniya me release nahi karte — pehle theek karte hain.

Netflix ki pipeline wahi hai: har code change pehle test screening se guzarta hai, phir chhote audience (canary) ko dikhaya jata hai, phir sabko. Aur chaos tools jaan-bujh ke problems create karte hain — taaki asli problem aane se pehle pata chal jaye.

2. Pipeline ke main stages

Guide ke hisaab se — planning se monitoring tak.

Planning — JIRA aur Confluence

Planning JIRA me hoti hai (tickets, sprints) aur documentation Confluence me. Har feature ka ticket hota hai, har decision likhi hoti hai.

Documentation isliye kyunki hazaaron engineers hain — koi bhi decision sirf kisi ke dimaag me nahi rehni chahiye.

Coding — Java (primary)

Backend services ki primary language Java hai (Page 71 me detail). Alag use cases ke liye alag languages bhi hain — lekin zyada tar backend Java + Spring Boot par hai.

Ek primary language ka fayda: hiring, libraries aur tooling ek jaisi rehti hai — har team alag language me nahi likhti.

Build aur Packaging — Gradle aur AMI

Build Gradle se hota hai, aur Netflix ne Gradle plugins bhi banaye hain apne use cases ke liye. Package karne ke baad code Amazon Machine Image (AMI) me pack hota hai — poora server image, dependencies ke saath.

AMI ka fayda: jo image test hui, wahi image production me chalti hai — “mere machine par to chal raha tha” wali problem khatam.

Testing — chaos tools se

Netflix testing par bahut zor deta hai — aur unke testing culture ka sabse famous hissa hai chaos tools (jaise Chaos Monkey): production me jaan-bujh ke servers band karo, dekho system kaise react karta hai.

Chaos engineering ka matlab: failure ka intezaar mat karo, use khud bulao — controlled tareeke se — taaki asli failure aane par system taiyaar ho.

Deploy — Spinnaker se canary rollout

Deploy Netflix ka apna tool Spinnaker karta hai — canary rollout: pehle 1% servers, phir dheere-dheere 100%. Agar error badhe to automatic rollback.

Spinnaker aaj open-source hai aur bahut si companies use karti hain. Canary ka matlab: naya code pehle chhote group ko, phir sabko.

Monitoring — Atlas aur Kayenta

Metrics Atlas me centralized hain — saari services ke metrics ek jagah. Kayenta canary analysis karta hai: naye version ke metrics ko purane se compare karke batata hai ki canary theek hai ya rollback karo.

Monitoring ke bina canary andha hai — pata hi nahi chalega naya code theek hai ya nahi.

Interview line: “Deploy karna aasan hai — deploy ke baad measure karna aur rollback karna hi asli CI/CD hai.”

3. Pipeline flow — ek nazar me

JIRA (plan) → Java code → Gradle build → AMI package
  → Tests (unit + integration + chaos)
  → Spinnaker canary deploy (1% → 10% → 100%)
  → Kayenta analysis (naya vs purana metrics)
  → Atlas monitoring (sab metrics ek jagah)
  → Error badha? → Auto rollback
StageToolKaam
PlanningJIRA, ConfluenceTickets + docs
CodingJavaBackend services
BuildGradleBuild + plugins
PackagingAMIPoora server image
TestingChaos toolsJaan-bujh ke failure test karo
DeploymentSpinnakerCanary rollout
MonitoringAtlas, KayentaMetrics + canary analysis

4. Try karo — ek deploy ki journey

Button dabao aur dekho Netflix par ek code change kaise production me jata hai.

5. Tools — ek table me

StageToolFayda
PlanningJIRA, ConfluenceHar kaam track + documented
CodingJavaEk primary language — tooling consistent
BuildGradleFast build + custom plugins
PackagingAMITested image hi production me
TestingChaos toolsFailure pehle se test karo
DeploymentSpinnakerCanary rollout + auto rollback
MonitoringAtlas, KayentaMetrics + canary analysis

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Canary ke bina seedha 100% deploy — ek bug se saare users affected. 2. Chaos testing ko ‘risky’ keh ke skip karna — controlled failure se hi pata chalta hai system kitna resilient hai. 3. Deploy ke baad metrics na dekhna — Kayenta jaisa analysis nahi to canary ka fayda nahi. 4. AMI ke bajay har server par alag build — ‘mere machine par chal raha tha’ wali problem wapas aayegi. 5. Rollback plan ke bina deploy — error badhe to wapas jaane ka rasta pehle se ready hona chahiye.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Netflix deploy ke liye kaun sa tool use karta hai?

  • Spinnaker — canary rollout ke saath — sahi jawab ✓
  • Jenkins hi sab kuch
  • Manual deploy

2. Chaos tools ka matlab kya hai?

  • Production me jaan-bujh ke failure create karke system ki resilience test karna — sahi jawab ✓
  • Code me jaan-bujh ke bug daalna
  • Server ko hamesha band rakhna
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: JIRA se plan, Java + Gradle se build, AMI me package, chaos tools se test, Spinnaker se canary deploy, Atlas/Kayenta se monitor. Deploy karna nahi, measure karke rollback karna hi asli CI/CD hai.

Original guide se — poori detail

Netflix ki CI/CD pipeline, stage by stage (guide se):

  • Planning: JIRA (planning), Confluence (documentation).
  • Coding: Java backend service ki primary language hai.
  • Build: Gradle; alag-alag use cases ke liye Gradle plugins banaye gaye hain.
  • Packaging: package aur dependencies ko Amazon Machine Image (AMI) me pack karke release karte hain.
  • Testing: production culture — chaos tools banane par focus.
  • Deployment: khud ka Spinnaker — canary rollout deployment.
  • Monitoring: metrics Atlas me centralized hain; anomalies detect karne ke liye Kayenta.
  • Incident report: incidents priority ke hisaab se dispatch hote hain; incident handling ke liye PagerDuty.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/netflix-tech-stack-cicd-pipeline.md
← PichhlaNetflix's Overall ArchitectureAgla →How TikTok Manages a 200K File Frontend MonoRepo
10Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

How TikTok Manages a 200K File Frontend MonoRepo

TikTok ka frontend TypeScript MonoRepo hai — 2,00,000 files ek hi repository me. Itne bade repo me Git clone karna bhi ghanton ka kaam ban jata hai. TikTok ne iske liye Sparo banaya — ek tool jo Git operations ko dramatically tez karta hai. Dekhte hain kaise.

1. MonoRepo kya hai? — ek almari wali kahani

Ek almari me saare kapde hain — sab kuch ek jagah, dhoondhna aasan, lekin almari itni badi ho jaye ki darwaza kholne me hi 10 minute lagen, to kya fayda? MonoRepo wahi almari hai: saare projects, libraries aur services ek hi repository me.

Fayde: code sharing aasan, dependency management simple, poora codebase ek nazar me. Problem: repo bada hote hi Git operations slow ho jate hain — clone, checkout, status — sab ghanton ka. TikTok ke 200K files par ye problem bahut badi thi.

2. MonoRepo ke fayde, problem, aur Sparo

Pehle fayde, phir problem, phir TikTok ka solution — Sparo.

MonoRepo ke fayde

Better code sharing — ek library banao, saare projects use karo. Simplified dependency management — versions ek jagah. Unified view — poora codebase ek jagah dikhta hai, cross-project change ek hi commit me hota hai.

Isiliye Google, Meta, Uber jaise bade log monorepo use karte hain — jab team badi ho to sharing ki value bahut zyada hoti hai.

Problem — bada repo, slow Git

Repo bada hote hi Git operations slow ho jate hain: clone karne me ghante, checkout slow, status slow. Developer ka time code likhne ke bajay Git ka wait karne me jata hai.

TikTok ka frontend TypeScript MonoRepo 200,000 files ka hai — yahan ye problem roz ki thi. Har naye developer ka pehla din clone ka wait karne me nikal jata tha.

Sparo — Git ko tez karne wala tool

TikTok ne Sparo banaya — ek tool jo bade frontend MonoRepos ke liye Git operations optimize karta hai. Iska idea: tumhe poora repo nahi chahiye — sirf wahi hissa chahiye jis par tum kaam kar rahe ho.

Sparo sparse checkout aur smart fetching use karta hai: sirf zaroori files lao, baaki on-demand. Result: Git clone aur operations dramatically tez ho gaye.

Interview line: “Scale par problem tool ki nahi, workflow ki hoti hai — poora repo clone karne ki zaroorat hi kyun hai?”

Sparse checkout — sirf zaroori files

Sparse checkout ka matlab: repo ke 200K files me se sirf wo files checkout karo jin par tum kaam kar rahe ho — jaise sirf /apps/feed folder. Baaki files disk par aati hi nahi.

Isse clone tez, disk kam, aur Git status bhi tez — kyunki Git ko kam files scan karni padti hain. Jab dusre folder ki zaroorat ho, to use on-demand lao.

Kab MonoRepo sahi hai, kab nahi?

Sahi hai jab: team badi ho, code sharing zyada ho, cross-project changes common hon. Galat hai jab: team chhoti ho, projects ka ek dusre se koi lena-dena na ho — tab alag repos simple rehte hain.

Lesson: MonoRepo ek trade-off hai — sharing ke liye tooling cost (Sparo, Bazel jaisi) chukani padti hai. Bina tooling ke bada monorepo sirf dard deta hai.

3. Sparo se pehle vs baad me

Git operationSparo se pehleSparo ke baad
ClonePoora 200K files — bahut slowSirf zaroori files — dramatically tez
CheckoutSaari files scan — slowSparse — sirf apna hissa
Status / PullHar baar poora repo scanChhota working set — tez
Disk usagePoora repo disk parSirf kaam ka hissa

Note: Guide me exact numbers diagram me hain — lekin direction ek hi hai: har operation pehle se kai guna tez. Sparo ka core idea “jo chahiye wahi lao” hai.

4. Try karo — ek naye developer ka pehla din

Button dabao aur dekho Sparo ke saath aur bina, ek developer ka pehla din kaisa hota hai.

5. MonoRepo vs Polyrepo

CheezMonoRepoPolyrepo (alag repos)
Code sharingAasan — ek jagah libraryMushkil — version sync karna padta hai
DependencyEk jagah manageHar repo me alag
Git speedBade repo me slow — Sparo chahiyeChhote repos — tez
Cross-project changeEk commit meKai repos me alag PR
Best forBadi team, shared codeChhoti team, independent projects

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Bina tooling ke bada monorepo banana — Sparo/Bazel ke bina 200K files ka repo sirf dard dega. 2. Poora repo har baar clone karna — sparse checkout use karo; jo chahiye wahi lao. 3. MonoRepo ko ‘hamesha behtar’ samajhna — chhoti team ke liye alag repos simple aur tez hote hain. 4. Sharing ke naam par har cheez ek repo me daalna — unrelated projects ka monorepo sirf confusion badhata hai. 5. Git operations slow ho to developers ko blame karna — problem workflow/tooling ki hai, developer ki nahi.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. TikTok ke frontend MonoRepo me kitni files hain?

  • 200,000 (2 lakh) files — sahi jawab ✓
  • 2,000 files
  • 20 files

2. Sparo ka main idea kya hai?

  • Sirf zaroori files lao (sparse checkout) — poora repo nahi — sahi jawab ✓
  • Repo ko delete kar do
  • Git ko band kar do
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: MonoRepo me sharing aasan hai, lekin 200K files par Git slow ho jata hai. TikTok ka Sparo sirf zaroori files laata hai (sparse checkout) — isiliye clone aur operations dramatically tez ho gaye. Bada monorepo bina tooling ke mat banao.

Original guide se — poori detail

TikTok ne apne 200K-file TypeScript frontend monorepo ke liye Sparo naam ka tool banaya. Sparo ke baad Git operations ke numbers:

  • Git clone: 40 minutes se sirf 2 minutes.
  • Checkout: 1.5 minutes se 30 seconds.
  • Status: 7 seconds se 1 second.
  • Git commit: 15 seconds se 11 seconds.

Monorepo ke fayde: better code sharing, simplified dependency management, code base ka unified view. Lekin monorepo jitna bada hota hai, Git operations utne slow hote hain — yahi problem TikTok ko face karni padi.

Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-tiktok-manages-a-200k-file-frontend-monorepo.md
← PichhlaNetflix Tech Stack - CI/CD PipelineAgla →Reddit's Core Architecture
11Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Reddit's Core Architecture

Reddit har mahine 1 billion+ users serve karta hai — posts, comments, votes, subreddits. Uske peeche ek architecture hai jo CDN se lekar load balancer, app servers aur databases tak faila hai. Is page me Reddit ka core map samjho.

1. Reddit ko samjho — ek sheher ka notice board

Reddit ek sheher ke notice boards jaisa hai: har mohalle (subreddit) ka apna board, log parchi chipkate hain (posts), dusre us par comment karte hain aur upvote/downvote karte hain. Sabse popular parchi sabse upar chipki rehti hai.

System ko chahiye: board jaldi dikhe (CDN + cache), nayi parchi turant sabko dikhe (real-time), aur vote ka hisaab sahi rahe (database). Reddit ka architecture yehi teen kaam karta hai.

2. Reddit architecture ke 5 hisse

Guide ke hisaab se — research par based, architecture badalta rehta hai.

CDN — Fastly sabse aage

Reddit Fastly CDN ko front me rakhta hai. Static assets (images, CSS, JS) aur popular pages CDN se serve hote hain — user ke paas wale server se, tez.

CDN ke bina har request origin server tak jayegi aur Reddit slow ho jayega. Popular post ko lakhon log dekhte hain — use baar-baar origin se serve karna waste hai.

Frontend — jQuery se modern stack tak

Reddit ne 2009 me jQuery use karna shuru kiya, phir TypeScript aaya, aur ab modern Node.js frameworks use hote hain. Android aur iOS ke liye alag mobile apps bhi hain.

Frontend ka evolution batata hai: architecture ek baar me nahi banta — har saal thoda-thoda badalta hai.

Load Balancer aur Application Stack

CDN ke peeche load balancer hai, jo requests ko app servers me baant ta hai. App stack me business logic hoti hai — post dikhana, comment karna, vote karna, subreddit manage karna.

Load balancer se ek server down ho to traffic dusre par chala jata hai — user ko pata bhi nahi chalta.

Databases — posts, comments, votes

Posts, comments aur votes ka data databases me store hota hai — relational + NoSQL ka mix, use case ke hisaab se. Vote counting aur ranking ke liye alag processing hoti hai, taaki har vote par poora page recompute na karna pade.

Hot posts cache me rehte hain — front page har second lakhon baar khulta hai, use DB se serve karna namumkin hai.

Real-time — votes aur comments

Reddit par vote aur comment turant dikhna chahiye — isliye real-time updates ke liye alag pipeline hoti hai. Naya comment aate hi subscribers ko push hota hai, page reload nahi karna padta.

Scale: 1 billion+ monthly users — is scale par har chhoti cheez (jaise vote count) bhi alag se design karni padti hai, nahi to database mar jayega.

Interview line: “Reddit ka sabse mushkil hissa vote counting aur ranking hai — har vote par poora front page dobara sort nahi kar sakte.”

3. Ek post ki journey — submit se front page tak

1. User post submit karta hai (mobile app / web)
2. Load balancer → app server
3. Post database me save + subreddit me add
4. Cache invalidate — subreddit ka page dobara banega
5. CDN: static assets serve karta hai
6. Dusre users: front page cache se dekhte hain
7. Vote aata hai → vote count update → ranking recompute (async)
8. Popular post front page par upar aa jata hai

Ranking ka funda: vote + time — naya post zyada votes ke saath upar, purana post dheere-dheere neeche. Har vote par ranking recompute karna mehenga hai, isliye batch/async me hota hai.

4. Try karo — ek post submit karo

Button dabao aur dekho tumhari post Reddit par kaise travel karti hai.

5. Architecture layers — ek table me

LayerTech / KaamKyun
CDNFastlyStatic + popular pages user ke paas se
FrontendTypeScript, Node.js, mobile appsModern stack, alag apps
Load BalancerTraffic baant ta haiEk server down ho to dusra
App StackBusiness logicPost, comment, vote, subreddit
DatabasesRelational + NoSQL mixHar data ke liye sahi store
CacheHot posts + front pageBina cache ke DB mar jayega

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Har request ko origin server se serve karna — CDN ke bina popular page bhi slow hoga. 2. Har vote par ranking recompute karna — async/batch me karo, nahi to DB mar jayega. 3. Cache invalidate bhoolna — naya post aaye to purana cached page dikhega. 4. Frontend ko ek hi stack me bandh dena — Reddit ne jQuery se TypeScript/Node.js tak evolution kiya; stack badalta rehta hai. 5. Real-time ko polling se karna — har second refresh karna server ko marega; push/websocket use karo.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Reddit apne front me kaun sa CDN use karta hai?

  • Fastly — sahi jawab ✓
  • CloudFront
  • Koi CDN nahi

2. Reddit par ranking update kaise hoti hai?

  • Votes collect karke async/batch me recompute hoti hai — sahi jawab ✓
  • Har vote par poora front page dobara banaya jata hai
  • Ranking kabhi update nahi hoti
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Fastly CDN aage, load balancer peeche, TypeScript/Node.js app stack, databases ka mix, aur cache + async ranking. 1 billion users ka raaz: popular cheez cache se, heavy kaam async me.

Original guide se — poori detail

Reddit ki core architecture (guide se) — har mahine 1 billion se zyada users:

  • Front: Fastly ka CDN application ke saamne hai; load balancer requests ko sahi services tak route karta hai.
  • Frontend history: 2009 me jQuery se shuru; phir TypeScript; ab modern Node.js frameworks; Android aur iOS apps bhi hain.
  • Backend shift: Python-based monolith se shuru, ab Go microservices ki taraf badh raha hai.
  • API layer: GraphQL heavily use hota hai. 2021 me GraphQL Federation shuru hua — chhoti GraphQL APIs (Domain Graph Services, DGS) ko combine karne ka tareeka. 2022 me GraphQL team ne core entities ke liye naye Go subgraphs add kiye, GraphQL monolith ko split kiya.
  • Data storage: Postgres core data model; load kam karne ke liye Postgres ke saamne memcached. Naye features ke liye Cassandra (resiliency aur availability ki wajah se).
  • Replication aur cache consistency: Debezium se Change Data Capture (CDC) process chalate hain.
  • Async work: voting ya link submit jaise expensive operations RabbitMQ se async job queue me daal kar job workers process karte hain. Content safety aur moderation ke liye Kafka se real-time data bhej kar rules chalate hain.
  • Hosting: AWS aur Kubernetes. Deployment aur infrastructure: Spinnaker, Drone CI, Terraform.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/reddit's-core-architecture.md
← PichhlaHow TikTok Manages a 200K File Frontend MonoRepoAgla →What is the Journey of a Slack Message?
12Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

What is the Journey of a Slack Message?

Tum Slack me message likhte ho aur ek second me dusre sheher me baitha teammate use padh leta hai. Beech me message 5 important servers se guzarta hai: WebApp, Admin Server, Channel Server, Gateway Server aur Envoy. Is page me us journey ko step-by-step samjho.

1. Slack message — dakghar wali kahani

Ek chitthi bhejte ho: pehle local post office (WebApp) use leta hai, phir sorting office (Admin Server) pata karta hai ye kis mohalle (channel) ki hai, phir mohalle ka dakiya (Channel Server) use register me likhta hai, aur phir har ghar tak pahunchane wala (Gateway Server) use deliver karta hai.

Slack ka message wahi karta hai — bas chitthi ki jagah bytes hain aur dakiya ki jagah servers. Aur kyunki channels lakhon me hain, Channel Server unhe consistent hashing se baant ta hai.

2. 5 servers — message ki journey

Slack ke real-time messaging framework ke hisaab se — har server ka kaam.

WebApp — client ka darwaza

WebApp wo API define karta hai jo Slack client use kar sakta hai. Tum message likhte ho to pehle WebApp ko request jati hai — ye entry point hai.

WebApp authentication aur basic validation karta hai: tum kaun ho, kis workspace me ho, message bhejne ki permission hai ya nahi.

Admin Server (AS) — sahi Channel Server dhoondho

Admin Server channel ID se pata karta hai ki is channel ka data kis Channel Server par hai. Lakhon channels hain — har channel ka malik alag server hai.

Ye routing ka kaam karta hai — bina iske client ko nahi pata hoga message kahan bhejna hai.

Channel Server (CS) — channel ki history

Channel Server channel ki history maintain karta hai — saare messages, kisne kab kya likha. Tum channel kholte ho to history yahin se aati hai.

Kyunki channels bahut zyada hain, Channel Server unhe allocate karne ke liye consistent hashing use karta hai — naya server aaye to sirf kuch channels shift hote hain, saare nahi.

Interview line: “Consistent hashing ka matlab: server add/remove ho to minimum data move ho.”

Gateway Server (GS) — WebSocket ka ghar

Gateway Server har geographic region me deploy hota hai aur WebSocket channel subscription maintain karta hai. Tumhara app Gateway se ek live connection khole rehta hai — naya message aate hi turant mil jata hai, refresh nahi karna padta.

Gateway isliye region-wise hai taaki connection tumhare paas wale server se ho — latency kam.

Envoy — cloud-native service proxy

Envoy service proxy hai — services ke beech traffic ko route karta hai, load balance karta hai, aur observability deta hai. Ye service mesh ka hissa hai.

Envoy se services ko ye nahi sochna padta ki dusri service kahan hai — proxy handle karta hai. Retry, timeout aur circuit breaking bhi yahin lag sakta hai.

3. Poora flow — message bhejne se padhne tak

Tum message likhte ho → WebApp (API + auth)
  → Admin Server: channel ID se Channel Server dhoondho
  → Channel Server: message history me save karo
     (consistent hashing se channel allocate hua tha)
  → Gateway Server: region ke hisaab se subscribers ko push karo
     (WebSocket — live connection)
  → Envoy: services ke beech traffic route karo
  → Teammate ka app: message turant dikh gaya ✓

Tum channel kholte ho → WebApp → Admin Server
  → Channel Server se history lao → dikhao

Consistent hashing kyun? Lakhon channels hain. Normal hashing me server add hote hi saare channels dobara allocate hote — consistent hashing me sirf kuch hi move hote hain.

4. Try karo — ek Slack message bhejo

Button dabao aur dekho tumhara message 5 servers se kaise guzarta hai.

5. 5 servers — ek table me

ServerKaamNa ho to kya hoga
WebAppClient API define karta haiClient ko pata nahi hoga kahan request bhejni hai
Admin ServerChannel ID se Channel Server dhoondhta haiMessage galat server par jayega
Channel ServerChannel ki history rakhta haiPurane messages nahi milenge
Gateway ServerWebSocket subscriptions (region-wise)Live updates nahi — baar-baar refresh karna padega
EnvoyService proxy — routing, LBServices ko khud routing karni padegi

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. History aur live delivery ko ek hi server se karna — Channel Server (history) aur Gateway (live) alag kaam hain. 2. Channels ko normal hashing se baantna — server add hote hi saara data move hoga; consistent hashing use karo. 3. Polling se real-time banana — har second refresh karna server ko marega; WebSocket use karo. 4. Gateway ko ek hi region me rakhna — door ke users ko latency hogi; region-wise deploy karo. 5. Message bhejte hi history bhoolna — naya user channel khole to use purane messages bhi chahiye.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Slack me channel ki history kaun maintain karta hai?

  • Channel Server (CS) — sahi jawab ✓
  • Gateway Server
  • Envoy

2. Lakhon channels ko servers par baantne ke liye kya use hota hai?

  • Consistent hashing — server add ho to minimum data move ho — sahi jawab ✓
  • Random allocation
  • Ek hi server par sab kuch
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: WebApp (API) → Admin Server (channel dhoondho) → Channel Server (history, consistent hashing) → Gateway Server (WebSocket push, region-wise) → Envoy (proxy). History aur live delivery alag servers par — isiliye Slack tez aur real-time hai.
