Top 9 Engineering Blogs

1000+ engineering blogs hain — kaun se padhne hain? ByteByteGo ke top 9 favourites: Netflix, Uber, Cloudflare, Meta, LinkedIn, Discord, AWS Architecture, Slack aur Stripe. Har blog ki apni khaasiyat hai — ye page batata hai kis blog se kya seekhne ko milega.

1. Engineering blogs — ustaadon ki diary

Engineering blog matlab hai: badi company ke engineers apni asli problems aur solutions likhte hain — kaun sa system kaise toda, kaise fix kiya, kya seekha. Ye textbook se zyada kaam ki cheez hai, kyunki ye real hai.

1000+ blogs me se 9 chunna mushkil hai — lekin ye 9 alag-alag cheezon ke liye best hain: scale, payments, network, messaging, data. Har blog ek alag ustaad hai.

2. 9 blogs — 5 tabs me

Har blog — kya seekhne ko milega, aur kyun padhna chahiye.

Netflix TechBlog aur Uber Blog

Netflix TechBlog — microservices, chaos engineering, EVCache, Spinnaker — scale par system kaise chalate hain, ye yahin se seekho. Is batch ke kai pages (64, 65, 67-69, 71) Netflix ke blogs par hi based hain.

Uber Blog — real-time dispatch, geospatial systems, Cadence workflows, aur CI/CD (Page 58). Uber ke blog se seekho: real-time system me latency aur reliability kaise balance karte hain.

Cloudflare Blog aur Engineering at Meta

Cloudflare Blog — networking, CDN, DDoS, aur internet kaise kaam karta hai — deep technical posts, diagrams ke saath. Network samajhna hai to ye sabse achha hai.

Engineering at Meta — duniya ke sabse bade scale (billions users) par systems: databases, caching, AI infra. Meta ke posts se seekho: scale par har chhoti cheez bhi alag se design karni padti hai.

LinkedIn Engineering aur Discord Blog

LinkedIn Engineering — Kafka (LinkedIn ne banaya tha!), data infra, aur feed ranking. Kafka aur data pipelines samajhne ke liye best.

Discord Blog — real-time messaging, voice, aur database migrations (MongoDB → Cassandra → ScyllaDB, Page 79). Discord se seekho: chhoti team badi scale kaise sambhalti hai.

AWS Architecture aur Slack Engineering

AWS Architecture Blog — cloud par system kaise design karte hain: reference architectures, best practices, cost optimization. Cloud seekhna hai to yahin se shuru karo.

Slack Engineering — real-time messaging framework (Page 75), scaling, aur reliability. Slack se seekho: message ek second me kaise pahunchta hai.

Stripe Blog — payments aur craft

Stripe Blog — payments, APIs, aur engineering craft. Stripe ke posts famous hain apni depth aur clarity ke liye — jaise idempotency, API design, aur incident handling.

Payment systems (Page 74) samajhne ho to Stripe + Shopify ke posts ek saath padho — theory aur practice dono mil jayenge.

Sahi tareeka: ek blog ko follow karo, roz ek post padho — 3 mahine me tumhari system design soch badal jayegi.

← PichhlaWhat is the Journey of a Slack Message?Agla →Uber Tech Stack
14Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Uber Tech Stack

Uber ka poora tech stack: web par Fusion.js, mobile par RIB + VIPER, beech me Uber Gateway (NGINX par, gRPC + QUIC), services me Spring Boot, uAct, Cadence, data me DocStore, Hudi, Pinot. Ek ride book karne ke peeche kitna kuch hai — poora map yahan hai.

1. Uber ka stack — ek sheher ki kahani

Uber ek sheher hai: sadkein (Gateway), traffic police (service mesh), godown (databases), aur control room (data processing). Rider app se “ride chahiye” kehte hi sheher ke saare hisse ek saath kaam karte hain — driver dhoondhna, price nikalna, route banana, payment lena.

Is page me har hisse ka tool samjho — frontend se lekar big data tak.

2. Stack ki 5 paratein

Guide ke hisaab se — Uber engineering blogs aur open-source research par based.

Web frontend — Fusion.js aur visualization.js

Uber ne Fusion.js banaya — ek modern React framework, robust web applications ke liye. Iske upar unke dashboards aur internal tools chalte hain.

visualization.js — geospatial visualization ke liye: map par cars, routes, heatmaps dikhana. Uber ka kaam hi location ka hai, isliye map visualization first-class hai.

Mobile — RIB cross-platform, VIPER architecture

Mobile ke liye Uber ne RIB banaya — cross-platform framework, aur architecture hai VIPER (MVC ke bajay). VIPER me har screen ke 5 hisse hote hain: View, Interactor, Presenter, Entity, Router — har hissa alag, testing aasan.

RIB alag languages me kaam karta hai: Swift (iOS) aur Java (Android) — ek design, do platforms.

Service mesh — Uber Gateway

Uber Gateway — NGINX ke upar dynamic configuration wala gateway. Client-server communication gRPC aur QUIC se hoti hai (tez, multiplexed), aur API define hoti hai Apache Thrift se.

Gateway se routing, auth aur rate limiting ek jagah hota hai — services ko ye sab khud nahi karna padta.

Services — Spring Boot, uAct, Cadence, Flipr

Java services Spring Boot par hain. uAct event-driven architecture ke liye hai — services events se baat karti hain. Cadence async workflow orchestration ke liye — lambi chalni wali processes (jaise trip lifecycle) ko steps me manage karta hai.

Configuration ke liye Flipr (baad me UCDP naam hua) — unified config store. H3 location-index library hai — duniya ko hexagon cells me baant kar location queries tez karta hai.

Data — DocStore, Hadoop, Pinot, AresDB

OLTP ke liye DocStore — strongly-consistent store, MySQL aur PostgreSQL ke upar, RocksDB engine ke saath. Big data Hadoop family se manage hota hai — file formats Hudi aur Parquet, cache Alluxio.

Time-series data Pinot aur AresDB me store hota hai — real-time analytics ke liye. Processing Hive aur Spark se hoti hai.

Interview line: “Uber ka stack batata hai: har layer ka apna tool — location ke liye H3, workflows ke liye Cadence, real-time analytics ke liye Pinot.”

3. Ek ride ki journey — stack se

1. Rider app (RIB/VIPER) → "Ride chahiye"
2. Uber Gateway (NGINX + gRPC/QUIC) → request andar
3. Dispatch service (Spring Boot) → H3 se paas wale drivers dhoondho
4. uAct events: driver ko request, rider ko updates
5. Cadence workflow: trip lifecycle (request → pickup → drop)
6. DocStore: trip record save (strongly consistent)
7. Pinot: real-time — abhi kitni rides chal rahi hain
8. Spark/Hive: raat ko analytics — surge pricing, demand forecast

4. Try karo — ek ride book karo

Button dabao aur dekho ek ride Uber ke stack se kaise guzarti hai.

5. Poora stack — ek table me

GatewayUber Gateway (NGINX), gRPC, QUIC, ThriftEntry point + fast communication

Config + LocationFlipr/UCDP, H3Unified config + hexagon location index

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Location ko normal database se handle karna — H3 jaisa spatial index chahiye; lat/long par simple query slow hoti hai. 2. Lambi workflows ko ek hi request me karna — Cadence jaisa orchestration chahiye, nahi to timeout aur partial state hoga. 3. Har service ko alag config dena — Flipr/UCDP jaisa unified config store rakho. 4. Real-time analytics ko OLTP database par chalana — Pinot jaisa alag store chahiye. 5. Gateway ke bina services expose karna — auth aur routing ek jagah honi chahiye.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Uber mobile apps kis architecture par bane hain?

  • RIB + VIPER — Swift (iOS) aur Java (Android) — sahi jawab ✓
  • MVC
  • Sirf web view

2. Uber location queries tez karne ke liye kya use karta hai?

  • H3 — duniya ko hexagon cells me baantne wala location index — sahi jawab ✓
  • Sirf MySQL
  • Google Maps API hi kaafi hai
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Fusion.js web, RIB+VIPER mobile, Uber Gateway (gRPC/QUIC), Spring Boot + uAct + Cadence services, DocStore OLTP, aur Pinot/Spark analytics. Location ke liye H3, workflows ke liye Cadence — har problem ka apna tool.

Original guide se — poori detail

Uber ke tech stack ki poori list (guide se):

  • Web frontend: Fusion.js (modern React framework); visualization.js (geospatial visualization).
  • Mobile: RIB cross-platform, VIPER architecture (MVC ki jagah); Swift (iOS), Java (Android).
  • Service mesh: Uber Gateway — NGINX par dynamic configuration; client-server communication gRPC aur QUIC se; API definition Apache Thrift se.
  • Service side: Flipr (baad me UCDP) — unified configuration store; H3 — location-index store library; Spring Boot (Java services); uAct (event-driven architecture); Cadence (async workflow orchestration).
  • Database: OLTP ke liye strongly-consistent DocStore (MySQL aur PostgreSQL, RocksDB engine).
  • Big data: Hadoop family; file formats Hudi aur Parquet; cache Alluxio; time-series data Pinot aur AresDB me.
  • Data processing: Hive, Spark, Marmaray (open-source data ingestion framework); messaging/streaming middleware Apache Kafka aur Apache Flink.
  • DevOps: Monorepo; devpod (simplified development environment); continuous delivery Netflix Spinnaker se; metrics uMetric me; alarms uMonitor par; consistent observability database M3.

← PichhlaTop 9 Engineering BlogsAgla →Twitter Architecture 2022 vs. 2012
15Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Twitter Architecture 2022 vs. 2012

10 saal me Twitter kitna badla? 2012 me Ruby on Rails monolith aur “fail whale” ka zamana tha; 2022 me microservices, distributed stores aur real-time pipelines. Ye page dono zamano ko aamne-saamne rakhta hai — diagram par based comparison.

1. 10 saal me kya badla? — ek sheher wali kahani

2012 ka Twitter ek kasba tha — ek sadak, ek dukaan, sab kuch ek jagah. 2022 ka Twitter ek metro sheher hai — highways, metro, alag-alag zones, aur har kaam ke liye alag department.

Badlav ek din me nahi aaya: pehle monolith toota, phir services bani, phir data stores badle, phir real-time pipelines aayi. Har badlav ek problem ka jawab tha — jaise fail whale (site down) se bachna.

2. 2012 vs 2022 — 5 hisse

Diagram ke hisaab se — har layer me kya badla.

2012 — Ruby on Rails monolith

2012 me Twitter abhi Ruby on Rails monolith se nikal raha tha — “fail whale” ka zamana, jab traffic badhte hi site down ho jati thi. Ek hi application me sab kuch — deploy slow, ek bug poora site gira de.

Us waqt scale: karodon users, lekin architecture abhi bhi simple thi — MySQL, Memcached, aur monolith services.

Shift — JVM (Scala/Java) ki taraf

Twitter ne backend ko Scala aur Java par shift kiya — Finagle RPC framework, aur services ko alag kiya. Ruby se JVM par jaane ka reason: throughput aur concurrency — JVM heavy load par behtar perform karta hai.

Ye shift saalon chala — monolith ko ek saath nahi toda, dheere-dheere services nikali (strangler fig pattern).

2022 — Microservices aur service mesh

2022 tak Twitter microservices par tha — har functionality ki alag service, apna deploy, apna owner. Service discovery, load balancing aur observability ke saath.

Microservices se teams independent ho gayi — ek team apni service deploy kare, dusri ko roke bina.

Data — Manhattan, Pelikan, Redis

Data layer bhi badli: Manhattan (distributed key-value store) tweets ke liye, Pelikan Cache aur Redis timelines aur counters ke liye, aur MySQL/PostgreSQL relational kaam ke liye (Page 60 me detail).

2012 me data ek jagah tha, 2022 me har data ki nature ke hisaab se alag store — polyglot persistence.

Real-time — recommendation pipelines

2022 me Twitter ke paas real-time recommendation pipeline hai — “For You” timeline 1.5 second me banti hai (Page 61). 2012 me timeline simple thi — followed logon ke tweets, time order me.

Ye badlav batata hai: product badla (discovery, recommendations), to architecture bhi badli.

Interview line: “10 saal ka badlav ek migration nahi — sau chhoti migrations hain, har ek ek problem ka jawab.”

3. 2012 vs 2022 — ek table me

Cheez20122022
ArchitectureRuby on Rails monolith (se nikal raha)Microservices
LanguageRubyScala / Java (JVM)
ReliabilityFail whale — traffic badhe to downDistributed, resilient
DataMySQL + Memcached, simpleManhattan, Pelikan, Redis, MySQL, Postgres
TimelineSimple — followed log, time orderRecommendation pipeline — 1.5s me “For You”
TeamsEk codebase, shared deployHar service ki apni team

4. Try karo — ek tweet, 2012 vs 2022

Button dabao aur dekho ek hi tweet dono zamano me kaise travel karta hai.

5. Badlav ke drivers — ek table me

BadlavWajahNateeja
Ruby → JVMThroughput aur concurrencyHeavy load par stable
Monolith → MicroservicesTeam scale + deploy speedIndependent teams
Simple DB → PolyglotHar data ki alag natureManhattan, Redis, SQL — sab apni jagah
Time-order → RecommendationsDiscovery aur engagement‘For You’ 1.5s pipeline
Fail whale → ResilientDowntime bardasht nahiDistributed + chaos-tested

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. 10 saal ke badlav ko ek migration samajhna — ye sau chhoti migrations thi. 2. Monolith ko ‘galat’ kehna — 2012 me monolith hi sahi tha; scale badla to architecture badli. 3. Language change ko magic samajhna — Ruby se JVM jaane se hi sab theek nahi hua; services aur data bhi badle. 4. Timeline ko sirf ‘database query’ samajhna — 2022 me ye ek ML pipeline hai. 5. Fail whale ko bhoolna — reliability ke liye architecture badli thi, sirf features ke liye nahi.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. 2012 me Twitter kis par bana tha?

  • Ruby on Rails monolith par — sahi jawab ✓
  • Microservices par
  • Sirf mobile app par

2. 2022 me ‘For You’ timeline kaise banti hai?

  • 5-stage ML pipeline — 500M tweets se 1500, 1.5s me rank — sahi jawab ✓
  • Sirf time order me
  • Random tweets dikhaye jate hain
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: 2012: Ruby monolith, fail whale, simple timeline. 2022: JVM microservices, Manhattan + Pelikan + Redis, aur 1.5s ML recommendation pipeline. Badlav ek migration nahi — sau chhoti migrations, har ek ek problem ka jawab.

← PichhlaUber Tech StackAgla →Netflix's Tech Stack
16Real-World Case Studies (Part 2)

Netflix's Tech Stack

Netflix ka tech stack — ek cheat-sheet: mobile Swift/Kotlin, web React, API GraphQL, backend Zuul + Eureka + Spring Boot, data EVCache + Cassandra + CockroachDB, streaming Kafka + Flink, video S3 + Open Connect. Page 68 me architecture thi, is page me stack ka har tool aur kyun — ek hi jagah.

1. Tech stack — ek toolbox wali kahani

Ek mistri ke paas ek hi hathoda nahi hota — hathoda, screwdriver, drill, aari — har kaam ka alag tool. Netflix ka stack wahi toolbox hai: har layer ka apna tool, aur har tool kisi khaas problem ke liye chuna gaya hai.

Is page ko cheat-sheet ki tarah use karo: interview me “Netflix ka stack batao” poochha jaye to yehi table suna do — har tool ke saath ‘kyun’.

2. Stack ki 5 paratein

Guide ke hisaab se — har layer me kya, aur kyun.

Mobile aur Web — Swift, Kotlin, React

Mobile apps native: iOS Swift, Android Kotlin — smooth video playback aur downloads ke liye. Web app React par hai.

Native isliye kyunki video player ko OS ke saath gehra integration chahiye — background playback, downloads, picture-in-picture — web view se nahi milta.

Frontend ↔ Server — GraphQL

Frontend aur server GraphQL se baat karte hain. Har client (mobile, TV, web) ek hi query me wahi data maangta hai jo use chahiye — over-fetching nahi, under-fetching nahi.

REST me har screen ke liye kai endpoints chahiye hote; GraphQL me client khud decide karta hai use kya chahiye.

Backend — Zuul, Eureka, Spring Boot

Backend Java microservices — Spring Boot par. Zuul API gateway (routing, auth, rate limiting), Eureka service discovery (kaun si service kahan hai).

Java isliye kyunki Netflix predominantly Java shop hai (Page 71) — hiring, libraries aur tooling ek jaisi rehti hai.

Databases — EVCache, Cassandra, CockroachDB

EVCache — distributed key-value cache, homepage aur sessions ke liye. Cassandra — viewing history jaise massive writes ke liye. CockroachDB — multi-region global transactions ke liye.

Detail Page 65 me hai — yahan yaad rakho: har data ke liye sahi store (polyglot persistence).

Messaging aur Video — Kafka, Flink, S3, Open Connect

Kafka — services ke beech events; Flink — real-time processing (recommendations, analytics). Video S3 me store, delivery Open Connect se — Netflix ka apna CDN, ISPs ke andar servers.

Open Connect hi wajah hai Netflix itna tez hai — video tumhare sheher ke ISP se aata hai, door ke data center se nahi.

Interview line: “Stack yaad karne ka tareeka: client → API → gateway → services → data → video. Har layer ek tool.”

WebReactComponent-based, live UI
APIGraphQLHar client apna data maange
GatewayZuulRouting, auth, rate limiting ek jagah
DiscoveryEurekaServices ke badalte addresses track karo
BackendSpring Boot (Java)Java shop — consistency
CacheEVCacheMilliseconds me lookup
DatabaseCassandra, CockroachDBWrites scale + global transactions
StreamingKafka, FlinkEvents + real-time processing
VideoS3 + Open ConnectStorage + edge delivery

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Stack ko bina ‘kyun’ ke yaad karna — interview me har tool ka reason poochha jata hai. 2. Page 68 aur 82 ko ek samajhna — 68 architecture (kaise jude hain), 82 stack (kaun se tools) hai; dono alag sawaal hain. 3. Ek tool ko har layer me lagana — GraphQL har jagah nahi, Zuul har jagah nahi. 4. Open Connect ko ‘sirf CDN’ samajhna — ye Netflix ka strategic advantage hai, ISPs ke andar servers lagana. 5. Java ko ‘boring’ kehna — Netflix dikhata hai Java scale par kaam karta hai.

7. Interview corner

8. Quick check

1. Netflix me service discovery kaun karta hai?

  • Eureka — sahi jawab ✓
  • Zuul
  • Kafka

2. Netflix videos kahan store hote hain aur kaise deliver hote hain?

  • S3 me store, Open Connect CDN se deliver — sahi jawab ✓
  • Sirf user ke phone me
  • YouTube se
Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Swift/Kotlin + React, GraphQL, Zuul + Eureka, Spring Boot, EVCache + Cassandra + CockroachDB, Kafka + Flink, S3 + Open Connect. Har layer ka apna tool — aur har tool ka ek ‘kyun’ hai, wahi interview me poochha jata hai.

Original guide se — poori detail

Netflix ke tech stack ki poori list (guide se):

  • Mobile aur web: Swift aur Kotlin (native mobile apps), React (web application).
  • Frontend/server communication: GraphQL.
  • Backend services: ZUUL, Eureka, Spring Boot framework.
  • Databases: EVCache, Cassandra, CockroachDB.
  • Messaging/streaming: Apache Kafka aur Flink (guide me "Fink" likha hai — ye Flink hi hai).
  • Video storage: S3 aur Open Connect.
  • Data processing: Flink aur Spark; visualization Tableau se; structured data warehouse ke liye Redshift.
  • CI/CD: JIRA, Confluence, PagerDuty, Jenkins, Gradle, Chaos Monkey, Spinnaker, Atlas.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/netflixs-tech-stack.md

Interview FAQs

12 FAQs — aaj ke era ke interviews me poochhe jaane wale sawaal, seedhe jawab ke saath. Sawaal par tap karo, jawab khulega.

01Netflix apni CI/CD pipeline me Spinnaker kyun use karta hai, aur canary rollout kya hota hai?
Spinnaker Netflix ka khud ka open-source deployment tool hai. Canary rollout ka matlab hai naya version pehle sirf 1% users par deploy karna, phir 5%, 50%, phir 100% — har step par Atlas metrics aur Kayenta anomaly detection dekhte hain. Agar naya version purane se alag behave kare (latency ya error rate badhe) to automatic rollback ho jata hai. Isse poora system ek saath risk me nahi padta. Uber bhi continuous delivery ke liye Spinnaker hi use karta hai.
02Uber ka tech stack — monorepo, Bazel aur Spinnaker ka combination kyun kaam karta hai?
Uber monorepo use karta hai — saara code ek repo me — taaki shared libraries aur cross-service changes aasan hon. Bazel bade monorepo ke liye fast, incremental builds deta hai (sirf badla hua code dobara build hota hai). Deploy ke liye Spinnaker canary rollout karta hai. Iske saath Flipr (config releases), uBuild + Buildkite (container packaging), aur uMetric/uMonitor/M3 (observability) mil kar ek poora platform banate hain. Interview me ye combination 'platform thinking' ka example hai — alag-alag tools nahi, ek coherent system.
03Twitter ki architecture 2012 se 2022 tak me sabse bada badlav kya tha?
Guide khud sirf ek line deta hai — 'What's changed over the past 10 years?!' — aur poori kahani diagram me hai. Diagram ke hisaab se Twitter monolith/Rails-based stack se microservices, real-time streaming aur modern data platform ki taraf badha. Interview me iska jawab diagram ko padh kar do: 2012 me simple monolith + MySQL jaisa stack tha, 2022 tak services, caching layers (Pelikan/Redis), Manhattan jaise custom databases aur stream processing add ho gaye. Is guide ka lesson ye hai ki architecture 10 saal me evolve hoti hai — koi design final nahi hota.
04Telegram ke normal chats end-to-end encrypted kyun nahi hote, aur secret chat kaise alag hai?
Telegram ke usual private aur group chats E2EE nahi hote — message server par encrypted store hota hai, lekin chunks aur decryption keys alag-alag countries me split karke rakhe jate hain, taaki hacker ko saare pieces ek saath chahiye hon. Secret chat E2EE hoti hai — message sirf receiver par decrypt hota hai — lekin uski limitations hain: group chat support nahi karta, normal one-to-one chat se alag hai, aur sirf mobile devices par enabled hai. Interview me ye trade-off bolo: convenience aur multi-device sync ke liye E2EE chhoda gaya hai.
05Stack Overflow sirf 9 on-premise servers par monolith me kaise chalti hai — microservices kyun nahi?
Stack Overflow ka poora traffic sirf 9 on-premise web servers handle karte hain, monolith architecture par, bina cloud ke. Interviewer ko microservices, sharding, event sourcing aur CAP theorem sunne ki ummeed hoti hai — lekin asal system iske ulta hai. Lesson: har problem ko distributed system ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Agar traffic aur data ek monolith me efficiently handle ho jaye to microservices ka operational cost bekaar hai. Interview me pehle scale aur requirements poochho, phir decide karo — 'microservices by default' galat approach hai.
06TikTok ne 200K-file monorepo ke liye Sparo tool kyun banaya, aur Git operations slow kyun hote hain?
Monorepo ke fayde hain — better code sharing, simplified dependency management, code base ka unified view. Lekin repo bada hote hi Git operations slow ho jate hain kyunki har operation ko zyada files aur history scan karni padti hai. TikTok ke 200K-file TypeScript monorepo me clone 40 minutes lagta tha. Sparo ne Git operations optimize kiye: clone 40 minutes se 2 minutes, checkout 1.5 minutes se 30 seconds, status 7 seconds se 1 second, commit 15 seconds se 11 seconds. Interview me monorepo ke trade-offs aur git internals (index, packfiles) ki samajh dikhao.
07Reddit ne Python monolith se Go microservices ki taraf kadam kyun badhaya, aur GraphQL Federation kya hai?
Reddit Python monolith se shuru hua, phir Go microservices ki taraf badha — Go ki concurrency aur performance ki wajah se. API layer me GraphQL heavily use hota hai; 2021 me GraphQL Federation aaya — chhoti GraphQL APIs (Domain Graph Services, DGS) ko combine karke ek unified API banane ka tareeka. 2022 me core entities ke liye Go subgraphs add karke GraphQL monolith ko split kiya. Data side par Postgres core model hai, memcached front me, Cassandra naye features ke liye, Debezium CDC se replication aur cache consistency, RabbitMQ async jobs ke liye, Kafka real-time moderation ke liye.
08Slack ka message 5 servers se kaise guzarta hai, aur Channel Server consistent hashing kyun use karta hai?
Slack message 5 servers se guzarta hai: WebApp (API define karta hai), Admin Server (channel ID se sahi Channel Server dhoondhta hai), Channel Server (channel ki message history rakhta hai), Gateway Server (har region me, WebSocket subscription maintain karta hai), Envoy (cloud-native service proxy). Channels ki sankhya bahut zyada hai, isliye Channel Server consistent hashing use karke millions of channels ko kai channel servers me allocate karta hai — naya server add hone par sirf kuch channels move hote hain. Receivers WebSocket (bi-directional) se real-time updates paate hain.
09Pinterest ne clone time 99% kaise kam kiya — shallow clone aur refspec me kya farak hai?
Pinterest ka Pinboard monorepo (350K commits, 20 GB, har din 60K pulls) clone karne me 40 minutes lagte the. Shallow clone (--depth 1) sirf latest commit leta hai, lekin Jenkins pipeline me phir bhi slow tha kyunki Git refspec option use nahi ho raha tha — har build pe 2500+ branches ke refspecs fetch hote the. Fix sirf ek line thi: refspec me 'master' branch specify kar di — clone 30 seconds ka ho gaya, 99% kam. Lesson: shallow clone history kam karta hai, refspec branches kam karta hai — dono alag optimizations hain, aur interview me dono ka farak batana chahiye.
10McDonald's ke event-driven architecture me Event Registry, Gateway aur MSK ka kya role hai?
McDonald's events standardize karne ke liye 4 components use karta hai: Event Registry (standardized schema define karta hai), Custom SDKs (events process karna aur errors handle karna), Event Gateway (identity authentication aur authorization), Utilities and Tools (events fix karna, cluster healthy rakhna, admin tasks). Scaling ke liye regional architecture AWS par global availability deti hai — producers events ko domain ke hisaab se shard karte hain, har domain ko ek MSK cluster process karta hai, aur cluster CPU jaise metrics dekh kar auto-scale karta hai (step-functions aur re-assignment tasks se).
11Netflix alag-alag kaam ke liye alag databases kyun chunta hai — EVCache, Cassandra, CockroachDB, Atlas aur Iceberg kab use hote hain?
Netflix 'one database for everything' nahi manta. MySQL billing/subscriptions ke liye, CockroachDB multi-region active-active transactions ke liye, EVCache (Memcached par, 10+ saal se) homepage aur recommendations cache karne ke liye, Cassandra default wide-column store (video/actor info, user data, device info, viewing history), Atlas open-source time-series DB metrics ke liye, Redshift/Druid analytics ke liye, S3 + Apache Iceberg unstructured/big data ke liye. Interview me ye bolo: database ka chunav access pattern aur consistency needs se hota hai, brand se nahi.
12Real-world case studies se interview me kya poochha jata hai — itne saare tech stacks kaise yaad rakhein?
Interviewer tool ke naam ratne ke liye nahi poochhta — wo ye dekhna chahta hai ki tumne trade-offs samjhe ya nahi. Har case study se 3 cheezein yaad rakho: (1) problem kya thi (scale, latency, reliability), (2) kaunsa pattern use hua (caching, sharding, event-driven, canary), (3) kyun wahi tool chuna gaya (jaise Netflix ne EVCache isliye chuna kyunki homepage data read-heavy hai). Tool ke naam bhool bhi jao to pattern yaad rakhna — 'cache-aside with Memcached' bolna 'EVCache' bolne se zyada important hai.
